fields.notes: At 22.01hrs MB came home drank and immediately started talking about GI doing drugs and going in and out of the house at night and keeping him awake whole night and he has to wake up early to go to work. I was trying to keep MB calm but he continuously our powered my talk. On Thursday morning GI never complained about it and GI and MB were both in the kitchen making a drink. At 22.30hrs CT's friend Charlie came down to wash his mug and MB started talking to him about GI and said "I am going to call police and he call 999 and pass the phone to Charlie. I was signalling Charlie to leave but MB kept talking to him and MB then asked for the house phone and call police from house phone   When MB was verbally threating to harm GI that time I call my on call manager at 22.50hrs and Juliet asked me to call police which I did Whiles I was on the phone to Police at 23.23hrs MB went to the back garden and got hold of GI jacket collar and brought him into the communal area and push him on the sofa. GI tried to get away from MB but he stood in front of GI. Whiles I was on the phone to police MB snatched the phone from me and that is when GI go up and went out of the front door.  Police arrived at 23.26hrs Incident No 0916.

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.notes:
PG:was reported to be in his room sleeping at the start  of day shift. PG woke up at around 10:45am and requested his medication from staff to which he was supervised while taking. Staff observed him to seem shaky and was very sweaty. Staff asked him if he was okay to which he said he was fine. At 11:15 he came running out of his room and told staff that he had been secretly drinking an excessive amount of alcohol to which he has now ran out of money and alcohol and is currently having withdrawals as he wasn't just meant to stop drinking straight away and go cold turkey, stating that it should of been a gradual process. He then went on to advise staff that he had contacted 111 to get advice about the current symptoms he was having ( Shaking and sweating) and they advised him to go to A&E at  Royal surrey hospital as it was an emergency and that his symptoms would progressively get worser and he was waiting for a taxi to get himself admitted stating he would potentially be back in a couple of days or longer. 

Staff asked PG if he knew what ward he was going to but he declined stating he would find out when he gets there and request for them to contact the house when they find out.  Shortly after getting dressed, he demanded to take all his medication stating he would bring it back when he was discharged.  

PG then proceeded to wait outside while staff engaged him in conversation and advised that they would be calling to check in on him and he also advised that he contact staff if they admitted him and the ward that he will be on. His Taxi arrived at 12:10 and he left on his way to the hospital. Staff called Royal surrey hospital at 14:26 and they confirmed that PG was at the hospital and was awaiting treatment and to be seen by a doctor.PG returned to the house at 17:40 and staff asked him how he was feeling, he told staff that he was feeling much better and gave staff his discharge summary. The doctor advised PG not to stop drinking abruptly as this can lead to withdrawal symptoms and was advised again to seek attention from i-access. At the writing of this report PG was in his room and he appeared fairly settled in his mental state.

Actions

•	Staff to encourage me to take my medication as prescribed and avoid skipping doses.
•	Staff to emphasize the importance of taking medication and the benefits of it keeping my mental state and mood stable
•	Staff to give regular updates to the community team about my presentation. To also contact out of hours in case of any crises.
•	Staff to document and fill in an incident form if I become verbally aggressive and threatening.

fields.subject: Brian Quilley Risk assessment
fields.notes:
I have a diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder, cluster headaches and substance misuse.
I have a history of feeling suicidal and I went to red hill train station and jumped on the train tracks, this resulted in my right leg Amputated at the knee. Due to my history of suicide. 
I am not consistent with my medication due to being intoxicated and will miss out doses. This leads to my mood to fluctuate, expressing suicidal thoughts to jump in front of a car, train, sending texts about a funeral.
A contingency plan was put in place, along with the police, me and social worker. This includes staff contacting me to see, if am safe. If I do not answer my call and it comes to 5 am, am to be circulated to the police.
The period I jumped in front of the train was in June and I tend to struggle during this month. My binge drinking increases during this time and during the festive season.

fields.subject: Brian Quilley Risk Assessment
fields.notes:
I am more prone to have an accident coming out of my wheelchair especially if I am intoxicated with Alcohol. I have been asked to use my prosthetic but insist on using the wheelchair. 
I am no longer able to go and play snooker as I am barred from the snooker hall because I attracted the police to the establishment causing concern for their image and reputation. 
Other residents have complained about me causing a nuisance when I return n intoxicated by shouting, singing and talking very loudly. This has been addressed with me and I have been told a warning may be issued as breach of tenancy. 
I admitted that I sometimes deliberately chooses not to take my phone or make contact due to feeling suffocated by the prospect of being “tracked”. Due to this my team agreed that it is in all’s best interest that I should not be reported missing to the police until 5am the following morning.
I also agreed that I will always ensure that I take my phone out with me and contact a staff member by call or text to let them know I am okay 
safety. I do not accept am vulnerability and that this is increased due to my physical impairments.
i cancel appointments for my learning to walk with Prosthetic leg.

fields.subject: LC Risk Assessment
fields.notes:
I am currently receiving a monthly depot injection at Guildford CMHRS . I am due for a medication 4/4/24, to discuss putting me on oral medication.  

I have previously had  problems but now drink alcohol on occasions.

I have  a history of using cannabis but am  currently using crack cocaine . I am also currently washing my own cocaine to smokable Crack to use. I am in contact with I-access and had my  first appointment on 15/01/24.
I am at risk of dying from misadventure due to overdose on cocaine.

I am aware that it’s against my tenancy agreement to bring alcohol or drugs on the premises, I might lose my tenancy if I do so.

Actions:
•	Staff to ensure that I attend my depot injection once a month. 
•	Staff to encourage me to be referred to drug and alcohol services.
•	Staff to address in regular 1:1 session the impact drugs have on my mental state.
•	Staff to address in 1:1 the impact of drugs on my physical health and risk of dying due to overdose.
•	Staff to contact emergency services when they find me unconscious due to risk of over dose.
•	To offer me regular 1;1 session to ventilate my feelings and thoughts.
•	Staff to assess my mood and mental state regularly.
•	Staff to be aware of my triggers/relapse signatures such as Isolation. 
•	Staff to contact  the crisis helpline, out of hours for support when incidents that are     unmanageable occur.
•	Update the community team of any changes in presentation and increase in risk /incidents.
•	When staff suspect that am using illicit substance on the premises , they are to redirect me and remind of how it affects my tenancy.
•	Staff to discourage me from giving others money to buy me drugs vice versa.
•	Staff to disengage they feel talking to me is not helping and my behaviours are escalating or intimidating them.
•	Staff to randomly check my bedroom for alcohol or drugs.

fields.subject: LC Risk Assessment
fields.notes:
I tend to leave the house at odd hours with others. The risk of doing so, especially around my safety have been discussed with me.

I have  a history of  with the police and have been to prison for 16 months for theft of a motor vehicle  -Several shoplifting arrests.
I tend to leave the house at odd hours of the night and  return early hours of the morning.  This places myself and others at the property at risk. The risks have been highlighted to me such as burglars coming to the house and anything happening to me whilst there.
I also spend time away from the house without communication with staff. Staff have to communicate via my friends  to know if am safe.
I have been encouraged to answer my phone and ensure it’s charged, so that staff can make contact to ensure am safe.

 I have been  banned from some shops and supermarkets such as Tesco for shop lifting. I need to gain insight of the consequences theft has on my future such as criminal record and going to prison.

I have been missing my court appearances which can result in arrest

I have not been taken my morning medication and declining to attend my depo injection appointment which can result to me relapsing

I have been making poor financial decision with my finances e.g. gambling and this can result in me losing my financial independence

I have not been attending my GP appointments, running away from the GP after checking in.
L have been diverting my uber from appointments going to unknown location.
I have been declining ambulance services when not feeling well
I have been declining support from staff to clean my room


Actions:
•	Staff to address in 1:1 sessions the impact re-offending has on my future.
•	Staff to explore causes that look at ways that can help me to stay away from re-offending.
•	Staff to contact the police if they observe with items that they suspect that I have stolen.
•	Ongoing risk assessments to be done.
•	Staff to remind me to let them know where am going and take a description of my clothing.
•	Staff to remind me of the mutual house agreements to try and return by 10pm and contact them if am running late.
•	Staff to remind of the risks associated with going out at odd hours.
•	To provide staff with information of where am going and answer my phone when they call me.
•	To circulate me to the police if staff are concerned of my safety and am not picking the phone.
•	To comply with the agreement in place, about leaving and returning at odd hours.

•	Staff to support me and remind me not to bring drugs on the premises.
•	Staff to remind me before the date and support me to attend.

fields.subject: BQ   Risk Assessment
fields.notes:
Sometimes when I’ve had a drink, or if I’m feeling unwell, I might not be able to get the bus home. I usually go out on my own and enjoy my independence, but I know that in some situations I might need extra support to get back safely.
If I can’t get the bus and don’t think to call a taxi, I could end up stuck or feeling vulnerable. I might not be thinking clearly if I’ve had alcohol, and that can make it harder to make safe decisions.

1.	What actions need to be taken to reduce risk? (Consider previous interventions which were helpful, and additional resources required)
I’ve saved local taxi numbers on my phone so I can call one if I need to. I’ve also agreed to give staff £40 to keep for me just for these situations. If I come home in a taxi, staff will pay the driver using the money I’ve given them.

How staff can support me:

Remind me that I can use a taxi if I’m struggling to get home.

Let me handle calling the taxi myself but be ready to support if I need help.

Use the £40 I’ve provided to pay the taxi when I arrive.

Let me know how much was used so I can top it up when needed.

Respect my independence but be there when I need help or reminders.

fields.subject: Behavioural Concerns
fields.notes:
Medication Monitoring: Ensure staff assist with consistent administration and track side effects.


Behaviour Support Plan: Create or review an individual plan focused on de-escalation techniques and personal triggers.
I had a conversation with my Visor Officer about some of my behaviour in the house. I was reminded that I need to take responsibility for myself, including going out to purchase my own cigarettes if I can't go without. We also spoke about a recent incident involving another resident, which led to the police being called. I understand that if someone comes back intoxicated, the best thing for me to do is to go to my room to avoid any conflict.

We also talked about my medication. I had stopped taking my depot injections because I felt they were affecting my motivation. However, I’ve been off them for a few weeks now, and I can see that I may be doing even less than before. I've agreed to restart my medication and planned to speak to staff about taking my tablet. I understand this is important for helping me stay on track.

I was also spoken to about some of my behaviour online and towards others. I admitted to wanting to approach people in an aggressive way and mentioned that I had sent a message to a female, saying I would get my sister involved. I now understand that this kind of behaviour is not acceptable, and I've been warned that I’m getting close to serious consequences. I know I need to take more responsibility for how I act.

I’ve agreed to re-engage with support, including taking my medication again. I’m also open to reflecting more on my actions and their consequences. I am working on staying calm, especially when things trigger me in the house.
’ve shown aggressive behaviour both in person and online, which has led to conflicts in the house. I stopped taking my medication, which caused a drop in my motivation and affected my mental health. There’s a risk I might react impulsively if triggers aren’t managed. However, I’ve acknowledged these issues and agreed to restart my medication and engage more with support.





Conflict Avoidance Strategies: Regular coaching on how to disengage safely from conflict situations.

Digital Safety Education: Provide support around safe and appropriate online communication; consider internet usage plan if necessary.

Regular Reviews: Weekly review with keyworker or mental health professional to monitor progress and adjust support.

Increased Supervision (if needed): If behaviour escalates, consider more frequent check-ins or supervised time outside the house.

fields.subject: BQ Community risk
fields.notes:
This raised an immediate concern due to BQ's known vulnerabilities, including hearing loss and a history of self-neglect. At approximately 02:58 AM, I was informed that a member of the public had found BQ lying on the ground near Tower Bridge, London. The Royal London Police were called to the scene and assessed BQ, who appeared to have visible injuries. An ambulance was called to provide further medical evaluation.

The police contacted us at Kingfield using our on-call number (07544 438874) to update us on the situation. They also informed us that Surrey Police had been made aware. Since BQ was without his hearing aids, I advised the officers to speak clearly and loudly near his ear to improve communication. I later called the police back to request the incident number and reference, but the officers explained that they did not have it immediately to hand and would need to refer to their notes.

Police confirmed BQ would be transported to Royal London Hospital in Whitechapel. They advised us to call the hospital for updates after 30 minutes. I called the hospital at 04:37 AM and was informed that BQ had arrived at 04:15 AM and was in A&E Zone D. Due to patient confidentiality, no further information could be shared at that time, and I was told to follow up in the morning.

On 30/05/2025 at 08:45 AM, I received a call from hospital staff at Royal London Hospital informing us that BQ had left the hospital without being formally discharged. This raised further concern for his safety. Later that evening, at around 08:15 PM, BQ returned to the residence. According to the night staff, he appeared fairly calm, was not under the influence of substances, made himself a meal, and went to bed without any signs of distress.

fields.subject: BQ
fields.notes: Since the incident on 29/05/2025, I’ve had time to reflect on what happened and how it affected me and the people supporting me.  I’ve spoken with staff at the residence about the situation, and I understand now why they were so concerned. I realise that being out for over 24 hours without letting anyone know was risky and caused a lot of worry.  I’ve agreed to wear my hearing aids more consistently, especially when I go outside, so I can better communicate and understand what's happening around me.  I’ve had a conversation with my social worker, who was updated about the incident. We discussed some of the reasons I left and ways I can ask for help next time instead of disappearing.  I’ve worked with staff to start putting together a personal safety plan. This will help me know what to do if I feel like I need space or am struggling to cope.

fields.subject: Additonal Notes and 1:1
fields.entry:
LS:
17:20- 18:30:
Staff arrived at the house at 17:20 and LS could be seen coming out of the outside toilet. LS appeared to be intoxicated or to have taken an illcit substance upon observation, Stafff asked him if he was okay to which he stated no and asked staff if he could speak to them. He expressed to staff that he didn’t feel safe at the property. When asked why he stated that he couldn’t really say why but he didn’t feel like the current environment was good for his mental health and he didn’t thing the people around him where a good influence. He also went on to ask about the house rules regarding drugs and alcohol to which staff reminded him of and he said that he didn’t see the point as he can go and do drugs and illicit substances outside. LS said that he wanted to move houses or go to a step-down service. He expressed that with a step-down service he thinks it will help him stop drugs as he would be on his own. Staff advised him that regardless of where he goes, he can only stop drugs and drinking for himself, and if it’s not something he genuinely wants to stop then it will be a constant cycle no matter where he goes. LS agreed with staff then went on to say he wanted an AA meeting but when him and staff checked there was none available until Saturday.  After this conversation LS briefly spoke to LC and staff. After LC had left the house, LS expressed again that there was something with LC that he couldn’t tell me had happened but if we could inform management that he wanted to move to a different location.  LS then went on to tell staff that he felt dirty so staff prompted him to go shower to which he originally declined saying he didn’t fell safe in the bathroom but after being reassured by staff he agreed to go and shower to which he was in there until about 18:30.

fields.subject: Care review
fields.entry:
10/07/2024 Luke engaged well in the meeting, however he clearly struggled to identify what he would like to do with his life and
evidently continues to struggle with pull towards crack cocaine. At times he found the conversation amusing which suggested he is not always
taking the current situation seriously, however he did evidence wanting to change and information from supported housing highlighted his ability
when not engaging in substances or with negative influences. We discussed what Luke wanted and the purpose of supported housing and he
was clear he wanted to stay and engage. Support from the supported housing to encourage Luke's continued engagement with IACCESS is
key, as well as building his confidence in himself and ability to say no. Agreed that review in three months was required to maintain momentum.
Support to be provided as well as pre-existing support is:
- creating vision board
- supporting Luke to attend sport in mind Badminton in Woking
- support Luke to find other sports activities locally, preference for basketball
- support Luke to think creatively about other activities - discussed going to the allotment to see if there is anyone he could support on their plot
if they are less physically able, could put sign up in allotment offering his support

fields.entry: At the start of the day shift, LS was reported to be awake in his room. At 08:14 am, LS informed staff that he received a call from the police about the incident of LC breaking his medication cabinet last month and the officer promised to visit him for further investigation. The police arrived at 08:30 am, he had a 1-1 interview with LS in the communal area and he later approached staff to know if the incident occurred. Staff confirmed that the incident occurred and mentioned the steps we had taken to safeguard LS from encountering such incidents with LC in the future. The police officer mentioned the incident at 17/06/2024 and gave the reference number: - 45240068144. At 08:58 LS went to get groceries at the local shop, and he returned to the house at 09:30 am. LS and LC were seen going in and out of the house during the day. At past 16:00 pm, staff and LS sat in garden, and he was lamenting that he has spent all his money on gambling as he was just left with £5. Staff then talk him through the adverse effect of gambling as there is no guarantee on return of the funds used in playing, he was sober and had a reflection on his action with a promise to stop gambling. LS was well engaged with staff and LC during the day. LS appeared to be a bit worried because of his financial loss due to gambling but his mentally stable during the shift. LS is in the room at the time of writing this note (18:29 pm).

fields.subject: TAP MEETING -07/08/2024
fields.entry:
Nathan is struggling in Wandsworth and has requested

for his solicitor to make a bail application. Jo has

spoken to Nathan and advised him that the

accommodation licence with Seacole is ending on 30th

August. Although there is option to reapply, she has

advised Nathan he could be homeless if released.

Nathan stated being homeless would be better than

being in Wandsworth.

It was felt that Nathan has not had a long enough

period of stabilisation and it would not be conducive for

him to be released now. Concern that he would

potentially just pick up same pattern of behaviour

where he left off. Nathan is used to Highdown, and is

feeling out of his comfort zone, and experiencing a real

dislike of prison. It is overcrowded, with no activities

being organised and they are spending a lot of time

locked up. Jo added that she is not getting impression

that Nathan is being intimidated or threatened, just that

he is not enjoying it in there.

Noted that Nathan still has 18 outstanding offences

which may impact whether bail is granted – however,

bed spaces are at a premium, system is strained due

to current civil unrest, and Nathan is not a risk to the

public as such so need to be mindful, he could be

released. Amy to request Nathan adds her to his visitor list; Jo and Amy to liaise for joint visit to see Nathan Any updates around request for bail to be shared once known.

Agency Actions / Updates

Substance Misuse:

Jo advised that Nathan said he is coming down on his

methadone – thinks it is around 40/45ml. He has been

free of pregabalin for a week. Liane has written to

healthcare about reducing his methadone and that

Nathan is keen to do this.

Jo voiced some concern that Nathan has intimated that

he has managed to get some Concerta in prison, not

officially. Jo has reiterated to Nathan that although he

wants to take Concerta for his ADHD, he needs to be

mindful of indulging in addiction type behaviours

around obtaining this. Everyone questioned whether

Nathan has actually been given Concerta, due to

national shortage, it is unlikely to have made its way

into Wandsworth.

Safeguarding Concerns:

Chenai questioned how Nathan is after self-harm

incident – Jo explained Nathan had a cut on his

forearm, which was not that deep. He did this because

he wasn’t happy in his cell with the other person, didn’t

get anywhere with request to speak to officer so did it

to get moved quickly. Jo has not known Nathan to self-

harm before and there haven’t been any further

fields.subject: Compliments
fields.entry:
Hi all

Naomi and I were blown away by the clean and tidy bedroom awaiting her on our return from the Cotswolds today. It was such a lovely surprise and both of us almost cried with joy! 

Naomi had been worrying about how/when to clean and tidy it, refusing my help, as usual. I was worrying about her returning to the mess and living like that again. 

She has been relatively clean and tidy whilst away and I hope this can be something of a fresh start for her. It's a real struggle for her to maintain self care, as you know, but with encouragement from all of us perhaps she can. I have been reminding her to wash her hands more regularly as well as to wash, rinse out or wipe clothes/bags that get messy - especially if they smell. 

I know that she can't always do this, and needs help, and I really appreciate your input to keep her safe and hygienic. 

Thank you again, so much,

fields.subject: DAILY NOTES
fields.entry: TW woke up at about 08:45hrs and had personal care. She took her medication supervised by staff then went to the cash point to withdraw her £110 allowance. She would be seen back after a few minutes as she was anticipating having a Medication review appointment with the pharmacist. She attended the resident house meeting.  TW was presenting anxiety as the GP had not specified the time of phone call. Staff reassured her and contacted the GP to enquire on the time frame, but they advised staff to expect a call after 12:30hrs as it was an afternoon appointment and had no specific time. However, the news agitated TW, and she was presenting anxiety and aggression as she had other plans for her day. Staff constantly reassured her, but she ended up screaming and shouting at staff then told them that she had enough waiting, and she was going.  At 12:20 TW went to the community to meet her friends. Manager (Juliet) supported TW by going to the GP in person to gather information about the medication review as TW needs her meds, but they advised to wait for the call from the pharmacist. TW was back at 16:40hrs and she appeared happy because she had been with her friend Ian. She would watch TV in the communal area then later went to her room where she remains at the time of the report.

fields.subject: Day Notes
fields.entry: MB was reported to be sleeping at the start of the day shift. At 09:45 am, MB came out of his room to greet the house Manager-Anita and staff on duty. MB then talked about the incident that happened a day before. MB explained that he only requested from the staff what was it that they are always writing about him, and he would want to have a copy of the notes. MB explained that he was not aggressive towards the staff, but the staff walked away while talking on the phone and went to spend the rest of the night in her car with the house door opened. MB mentioned that he reported it to the police and locked the door as other residents thanked him for keeping the door locked. MB left the house to town at 10:37 am and returned to the house at 15:30 pm. Jo- Social worker called the house manager-Anit to inform her that MB was intoxicated, angry and even used his bicycle to hit a fence while away from the house today and that she would want a male staff to be on duty throughout the night in other to keep the situation under control. When MB arrived at the house at 15:30 pm, he then informed the House manager that Christmas season is a period that he grieves the lost of his brother and he would not want any staff to ask about how is doing or feeling as that triggers his emotion, but he would prefer to be left alone. MB mentioned that if he needs help, he will ask from the staff or call the crises team -111. MB also requested that he want the management to investigate the incident and give him an update or outcome of their investigation, the house manager-Anita reassured him that he would be updated. At 18:00 pm, MB came out to have a smoke in the garden, he informed staff that he would be visiting his Mum tomorrow and her sister. MB then returned to his room, he appeared to be mentally stable and calm in his mood at the time of writing this note (18:26 pm).

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.entry: NP was reported to be sleeping at the start of the day shift. NP woke up at past 09:00 am, greeted staff, use the bathroom and returned to his room. At 10:00 am, he approached staff and mentioned that his funding has being approved for rehab. Staff reminded him of his outstanding Utility bill, he said his dad will pay it, later he requested staff to issue him a payment receipt of £75 today for him to give it to a friend that will credit the account. Staff handed over to him the outstanding bill issued by finance, but he grumbles that he wants a receipt of payment for £75 and staff declined to that request since he did not make the payment. At 10:20 am, staff prompted him for his medications, and he used it. NP left the house into the community at 10:50 am and he returned to the house at 11:25 am. NP left the house again at 13:30 pm, to Addlestone and he returned to the house at 15:45 pm. Incident: ‘‘NP was in his room at 15:50pm, staff heard him talking on the phone and later he began to shout, and staff heard sound in his room. NP continued to shout, staff and LC rushed to his door and forced it open. NP was found sitting on the floor with broken plastic plate beside him and he could not stand up. Staff and LC supported him to get to sit properly on the bed. NP tried to stand-up, but he was staggering and shouting in usual manner while speaking to someone called Dan on the phone. Staff immediately called the emergency services as his speech was not coherent. NP shouted that staff should not call the ambulance as he refused to speak with the emergency services agent. He said staff should leave his room that he would be fine, but staff was guiding him not to fall. The emergency services promised to send ambulance and stated that it might take up to 4 hrs before their arrival. At 16:15pm, he came out of his room and said he found a substance at Addlestone bridge which he thought it was Cocaine, but it was Ketamine, and he used it. NP told staff that he needs to go out of the premises to get fresh air and he would be fine. At 16:20 pm, staff heard him calling a friend and he gave the postcode of the house to the person. Staff persuaded him to sit down and relax instead of going up and down the premises. At 16:33 pm, he left the house with Luke Clement into the community and NP told staff that he would be fine’’. At 17:25pm, NP returned to the house, and he was heard speaking on the phone at the back garden. At 18:03 pm, NP called the house, and he was apologising to staff that he did a wrong thing by using the substance and he was recapping the incident at the time of event. At 18:17 pm, the emergency services called the house phone number to speak with NP, he answered and said his fine that he does not need their services. NP appeared to be calm in his mood and mentally stable as he remained in his room watching TV at time of writing this note (19:01 pm).

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.entry: NP was reported to be sleeping at the start of the day shift. It was reported during handover that he was intoxicated before going to bed last night, so staff checked on him at 08:07 am, and he was found breathing and stretching at that time. NP woke up at few minutes before 09:00 am, he went to use the bathroom and returned to his room. At 09:20 am, NP left the house for about 45 minuets and when he returned, he appeared to be annoyed as he was complaining about LC and WBM causing disagreement between him and his friends. He was paranoid as he was unable to get through to his friend on the phone, then he began to call out WBM and verbally abusing him that they have betrayed his trust. Staff cautioned NP to stop abusing other residents and deescalated the issue between them. When LC returned to the house at 13:21 pm, NP engaged LC, and they settled their differences. Staff asked NP about the cheeses that was seen on the floor in the communal area, he denied splashing off WBM cheeses from his plate. Staff reiterated to them that residents are no longer allowed to enter each other’s room, and he was giving a letter on the breach of house agreement as regard using of substances and drinking of alcohol on the premises. Staff supported NP to clean him room and he handed over lots of syringes and needles to staff with a teaspoon powdered substance which was seized. NP said he does not want to get involved in using any substances in other to prepare for his detox. NP left the house at 16:57 pm that he was going to see a friend and that he would likely be back on Friday. At 17:25 pm, NP called the house phone that he is considering going to stay with his brother to avoid having any issues with other residents for now. At the time of writing this note, NP was reported to be away from the house(19:21pm).

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.entry: LC was reported to be hospitalized at the start of the day shift.  At 10:41 am, staff called St’ Peters Hospital to report that an empty bottle of Concerta 18mg was found in his room and that was noted by the personnel of the hospital. At 12:20 pm, staff received a call from St’ Peters Hospital to book LC Uber to return to the house. At 13:21 pm, LC returned to the house, thought he appeared fragile, and he mentioned that he took excess drugs of Xanax yesterday. LC was then seen with NP settling their differences. LC then sat in the back garden while trying to smoke he vomited, and staff supported him to clean up. LC later went to get food and sat in the communal area to talk with NP and staff, but he appeared to be dull. LC mentioned that he would need to go into his room to sleep but might need a bowl beside him in case he might want to throw-up. Staff supported him during the day to clean up his room and he appreciated that. At 19:40 pm, staff checked up on him in his room and he responded that’s fine.

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.entry: WBM was reported to be sleeping at the start of the day shift. WBM woke up at past 11 am, when he heard NP verbally abusing him and mentioning that LC was in WBM room before coming to his room yesterday. At 11:40 am, staff prompted him for his medications, and he was observed taking the medications. NP continued to be aggressive verbally towards WBM that he does not have LC back and calling him all sorts of name, staff deescalated the issue by redirecting NP from talking to WBM. At 13:15 am, WBM went to prepare his food (Bread and Cheeses) to eat in the kitchen and he reported that NP splash off some of his cheese on the floor. Staff cautioned NP but he denied splashing off WBM’s cheese and said staff should check the CCTV to see what transpired between them. WBM reported to his mum that NP was bullying him and calling him all sort of names. Staff spoke with the mum and explained that both WBM and NP had disagreement though this has been deescalated and the mum was reassured that things are under control. Staff gave WBM a warning letter on breach of the house agreement which relates to the use of substances and alcohol on the premises or residents going into each other’s room. At 15:30 pm, staff supported WBM with his afternoon medication and he was observed while taking it. WBM remained calm in his mood and mentally stable during the day shift. WBM remain in his room at the time of writing this note (18:51 pm).

At 22:03 LC started arguing with NP and shortly got physical and started fighting. Staff contacted 999 and WBM intercepted, and they stopped fighting. Police asked questions as they analysed the situation on phone and when staff informed them that they had stopped fighting, they said they would not come over but if they start fighting again or feel unsafe staff should call them immediately. (Case reference number is SYP-2024127-0796). Staff asked LC if he was ok, and he said he was ok but wanted to be left alone. LC went out with NP and WMB at 22:39 and came back at 22:56 he appeared to be calm, and he went to his room to sleep. LC went out at 02:50 and came back at 03:02.  By morning LC appeared to be mentally settled and calm in his moods. At the time of writing this report LC was in his room sleeping.

fields.subject: Night notes

He said “I look out for you, I do things for you; I support you, give you clothes and much more but you pay me back by stealing from me” LC shot/shouted back at him, and they started fighting from the corridors and went downstairs. Staff called 999, WBM intercepted, and they stopped. Police asked questions as they analysed the situation on phone and when staff informed them that they had stopped fighting, they said they would not come over but if they start fighting again or feel unsafe staff should call them immediately. (Case reference number is SYP-2024127-0796) NP told staff “We are ok, we don’t need police, we sorted everything already” NP went out with LC and WMB at 22:39 and came back at 22:56. NP went to his room, he spent time talking on phone, he could get agitated and then laugh at some instances, NP sounded like he had mixed feeling.  he would later go to sleep and stayed in his room till 03:30 when he woke up and expressed that it was too cold. He went to the lounge and laid at the couch. NP seemed to be agitated during the early hours of the night but appeared to be fairly settled and calm in the morning. fields.subject: BQ 's Care review
fields.entry:
BQ’ had an   appointment on 07.01.25 with his Social worker and his Key worker from I-Access. The i-Access's goal was to discharge him today from their services and sessions since he initially was on alcohol reduction sessions. Seeing that his behaviour on alcohol has been increasing they reconsidered le to keep him open considering he will consider abstinence and follow their safe reduction plan. The agreement was that he will now start sessions on alcohol abstinence online and they will share the link with us for him to attend and staff should encourage and prompt him to attend these sessions once in two weeks. It was agreed that if he missed two sessions they will cancel and discharge him from their services as he is expected to comply. He has an appointment wat ST George on the 9th of January he will go with Emmanuel staff. We ordered his hearing aids so that he can be able to communicate on Thursday when he goes for his appointment.  Hannah his social worker gave an update of the new proposed accommodation, and she will be picking him up on Friday 10th January to go and view the property. She strongly emphasised to him not to raise his hopes as this triggers him to misbehave whenever the outcome doesn't favour him. She indicated that they are trying their best to move him and   the accommodation that they are going to view is not 100% verified and certain that he can move because there is still need for the team to negotiate clearance since the costs will be high. We also discussed about his on-going behaviour and alcohol intake that has also affected his health as he looks deteriorated. Hannah spoke to him strongly that Staff should report him for his racial abuse and that seacole should do disciplinary procedures for BQ and report his intolerable behaviour to police. She apologized on behalf of surrey team to all staff on what BQ has put them through.  warning letter was sent when she had left however i will ask Night staff to print it and hand it over to BQ since the printer is not working i did not print it during the day. 



Staff supported BQ on 09.01.125 to St George hospital for his appointment. He was referred for an XRAY first then went to see DR Lucy. She engaged him asking BQ based on the 2006 records asking how his leg was being treated. He responded to say he was being treated brilliantly. She went on to say the Xray result shows that the leg is all right however seeing that he continues to complain with the pain she suggests that BQ should do further scans like CT scan, MRI scan and blood samples. We went to do blood samples, and they will set an appointment for scans and communicate as usual. Currently the X-Ray shows that there is no infection however should they do the scans they may get clarity maybe there might be infection in the bones, and they can decide if there is further surgery that can be done. The doctor commended him for looking fit, good and healthy. She also advised him that is he is feeling unwell anytime he should come to that hospital.

PG:was reported to be in his room sleeping at the start  of day shift. PG woke up at around 10:45am and requested his medication from staff to which he was supervised while taking. Staff observed him to seem shaky and was very sweaty. Staff asked him if he was okay to which he said he was fine. At 11:15 he came running out of his room and told staff that he had been secretly drinking an excessive amount of alcohol to which he has now ran out of money and alcohol and is currently having withdrawals as he wasn't just meant to stop drinking straight away and go cold turkey, stating that it should of been a gradual process. He then went on to advise staff that he had contacted 111 to get advice about the current symptoms he was having ( Shaking and sweating) and they advised him to go to A&E at  Royal surrey hospital as it was an emergency and that his symptoms would progressively get worser and he was waiting for a taxi to get himself admitted stating he would potentially be back in a couple of days or longer. 

Staff asked PG if he knew what ward he was going to but he declined stating he would find out when he gets there and request for them to contact the house when they find out.  Shortly after getting dressed, he demanded to take all his medication stating he would bring it back when he was discharged.  

PG then proceeded to wait outside while staff engaged him in conversation and advised that they would be calling to check in on him and he also advised that he contact staff if they admitted him and the ward that he will be on. His Taxi arrived at 12:10 and he left on his way to the hospital. Staff called Royal surrey hospital at 14:26 and they confirmed that PG was at the hospital and was awaiting treatment and to be seen by a doctor.PG returned to the house at 17:40 and staff asked him how he was feeling, he told staff that he was feeling much better and gave staff his discharge summary. The doctor advised PG not to stop drinking abruptly as this can lead to withdrawal symptoms and was advised again to seek attention from i-access. At the writing of this report PG was in his room and he appeared fairly settled in his mental state.

CE appears calm in her room when the shift commenced. She was heard talking on her phone telling someone about “witness” and she seemed a bit worried at first but staff later heard laughing. Staff prompted her about delivery man waiting for her. She collected her pizza and a bottle of coke and returned to her room. She used the bathroom and left her bowl in the sink and told staff that she will wash it later. 
CE was prompted at 9:55pm for her medication but she declined. She was prompted again at 10:57pm and she still declined and said staff should leave her alone. She was observed through her window watching her phone at 12 midnight. She was heard at 00:50hrs talking but staff was not sure if she was on the phone. 
CE was observed many times through her window and she was not sleeping. She was seen lying on her bed around 2am to 4am. She used the bathroom around 4:50am then approached staff for her medication.  She took it to her room and staff followed her. She asked staff why and staff told her she can’t document it until staff has witness her taking it. She then took it at 5am. She showed staff a knife and said she will harm herself. Staff asked if she would like to speak to the crisis team but she declined. Staff gently asked her to give her the knife back but she laugh and declined. She asked staff if she will call the Police and staff said no. She was encouraged to sit with staff and talk about it. She said she has been hearing voices and if she stab herself, it make her happy. She then asked if the manager JM will be here today and staff told her she is not sure.  Staff asked if she will be going for training today and she said no. She told staff that a staff member of staff told her that she will be going to the prison and staff said she is not aware. She told staff she likes to stay here instead. She was kept engaged for few minutes and CE told staff that she would like to watch a movie in her room. She complained about not been able to sleep and staff asked if she would like to take her PRN but she declined. She did her oral hygiene at 5:16am and returned to her room. Staff tried to make a call to the crisis team but the phone keypad won’t type number 0(prefix).
CE was observed watching a movie her phone through her window. She turned off her lights and was heard singing along a music that she was playing at around 6:56am. She remains in her room and appears content when the notes were updated.

fields.subject: Day Notes
fields.entry:
PH 
At 8:36, PH woke up and went for a cigarette. He appeared calm and didn’t seem bothered by the new staff. However, he has a severe cough when he smokes. At 8:42, staff assisted him with his medication and noted that he had run out of some medications from the smaller boxes.
At 9:00, staff prompted PH to have breakfast, which he agreed to, and he had a bowl of cereal. Staff also reminded him to go food shopping, and he said he would go later in the day. 9:10, PH appeared agitated, pacing up and down the house and shouting phrases such as, “I have no brain.” Staff administered his PRN medication to help settle him.
At 9:15, PH changed into a blue hoody, a grey jacket, blue jeans, and walking/hiking trainers before heading outside, only to return five minutes later. He continued to talk to himself, saying things like, “Everyone thinks I’m a paedophile,” “You’ve always had a brain,” “Exposing yourself,” and “She said no, and that’s that.”
At 9:40, PH was still talking to himself, mentioning “Tesco’s” before leaving the house. At 10:43, PH returned with a small bottle of milk and a ready meal. At 11:10, PH attempted to prepare the curry and rice ready meal but struggled with the microwave. Staff stepped in and assisted him in reheating the meal.
By 11:30, he was still pacing in and out of the house and his room. At 11:45, PH came out of his room, claiming his bank card had been stolen. He thought someone had taken it from his room. Staff reassured him and offered to help him search for the card.
Throughout the morning, PH spent a lot of time walking in and out of the house. From 12:30, he seemed more settled, talking less to himself and frequently going into the garden to smoke.
At 13:30, PH came out of his room, still calm, and asked about his bank card. He asked staff to help him contact Barclays, which they did. However, he was unable to provide all the necessary ID details to access his bank account, so Barclays advised him to visit the branch in person on Monday. PH remained calm and seemed to understand this explanation.
The Home Treatment Team contacted staff to inform them they would be visiting PH later that afternoon. At 14:50, Will from the Home Treatment Team arrived to visit PH and bring his new medication. He attempted to engage PH, but PH was reluctant to fully interact. As a result, HTT staff asked PH about his sleep the previous night, and he reported going to bed at 10:00 pm and waking up at 6:15 am, as noted in the handover.
At 16:45, PH was still asking about his card, so staff assisted him in searching his room again, though the card was not found.

fields.subject: Night Notes
fields.entry:
NIGHT NOTES: MB
MB was reported to be in his room when the night shift commenced. He came out of his room holding a glass of beer. He went to the kitchen, and he went back to his room. After few minutes he went to use the bathroom, could hear him shouting at 20:51 and he went back to his room. He was in and out of his room.

At 22:43 he came and stand on the door of the lounge, he appeared drunk, and he said ooh this idiot is still here on the sofa. Could hear him talking and sometimes shouting. He was talking on the phone but could not hear clearly what he was saying because of the music he was playing was so loud in his room. Soon after 23:00 he came with is phone in the lounge and he said to staff speak to her now, come on tell her everything, explain to her what is going on. Staff tried to ask MB who was on the phone and what was the issue the staff needs to explain and why. He could not give the staff a chance, or answer he keeps on insisting that they have to speak to the person on the phone. After few minutes MB shouted it is my sister.  Staff could not hear her clearly because MB was shouting standing close to staff, and he was saying I am complaining about this boy pointing to TM. He said this bustard is always sleeping on the sofa and he is getting all the attention he wants because he is in the lounge near the staff doing nothing. He started calling TM names he said you are an idiot, black monkey, why are you here all the time, at that time he was still point to TM in his face. 
Staff tried to stop and remind MB that he must not shout or verbally abuse other residents, and staff reminded MB that he is on bail because of another incident, so he must not speak to TM for now but could not listen. He grabbed his phone, and he walk away. Staff called the police and reported the incident and in the middle of it. AN ambulance approached the premises, and they said MB called them earlier. Staff explained to police that there was an Ambulance, and they said if there are any serious issues when the ambulance left staff must call them again.
The paramedics assessed MB and they said he wants to go to hospital and see, a mental health Doctor, and they left. Staff called the on – called manager and notify her. And she advised that since he has gone to hospital staff need to report on Online Surrey police report. Staff reported the incident.
MB is not back yet at the time of this report.

fields.subject: Communication from PC Laura
fields.entry:
Good morning Pippa,

Yes we still are, I have checked our system and we have an interpreter booked for 1030hrs. I’ll be explaining to CE that the investigation has been handed over to the Romanian Police and we will not be doing a video recorded interview at the moment.

I have considerable concerns about doing the VRI, as does my reviewing supervisor. Whilst she has maintained she wants to do one, every time we have come close to it, it has triggered a significant mental health episode. I have tried explaining this before by phone to CE. I know she wants to do one, but I have arranged the intermediary assessment (necessary before the interview) several times and each time she has needed to cancel. In our opinion, her mental health needs to be the priority and continuing to attempt to do something that is going to put her at risk is not something we can keep doing. If / when her mental health improves to a point where it would be safe to try, then we can revisit it.

fields.subject: Communication from Jo - support worker
fields.entry:
I have spoken with Matt this afternoon.  He said he is now out of hospital and back at home.  Asked if and when he would like to meet but didn't really give me straight answer stating that I said I did not feel safe around him.  I reminded him of the conversation that I am still working with him but will not take him in my car when he highly under the influence but happy to meet him out or here at GA.  Is is adamant that he needs to make no changes to his behaviour and insits that he is only being evicted "because they don't like me and I am the wrong colour"  I have explained again that the reason for eviction is due to his behaviours towards staff and residents and because of increasing arrears - he wishes to address neither and strongly believes that he is not at fault and bares no responsibility about being rehoused.
 
Said he has been given an appointment with Iaccess tomorrow but wont go as he has probation and that he didn't make the appointment himself anyway.  I have suggested he call to rearrange but again he seemed reluctant to work with them any way.
 
I am aware that we all through that there was a strong possibility that he would be back before court now with regards to the breech of his SSO but this isn't the case. We have 20 days until he is street homeless, are there any other action that we should be taking at this stage.  Is it still Runneymede council he will need to present to as homeless if we get that far?
 
He has told me "if they are going to piss me off I will piss them off" and has threatened to smear excrement over the walls of his room the day he leaves.
 
Although I am very tempted to plan to go and see him to see if we can help diffuse the current situation I don't think that it will currently have any impact and I want him to be very clear with the boundaries at the moment.
 
It will be interesting to see if he attends his probation appointment tomorrow.

fields.subject: Update from Probation - Lewis
fields.entry:
I have just out of an appointment with Matthew which was very long but I have to say very productive. We spoke at length about everything going on at this time. He was accepting a lot of responsibility but of course trying to shift some blame, which I could challenge him on. He was respectful throughout and was not heavily under the influence. He was even tearful at times thinking he has sabotaged so much and damaged his relationships with staff. He seemed to minimise his behaviour but I had him up on that in terms of how abusive he has been and he seemed to listen.

 

He seemed adamant he is going to engage with alcohol treatment and will go to a detox facility if offered.  I reaffirmed this several times and we want to coincide I-Access with Probation next week. There was also suggestion from Matthew as to whether Jo from Guildford Action would come to an app with him to try and started rebuilding working relationships.

 

Our Accommodation Officer was also in on the appointment and spoke to Matthew about a Duty to Refer but tempering his expectations given the current circumstances.

fields.subject: Update from PC Laura
fields.entry:
Myself and Pippa visited Claudia yesterday along with a Romanian interpreter. She explained what happened with the Romanian police when she last returned, and talked about the other investigation the Metropolitan police have. She also showed us her letter about trial in June 2026. 
Pippa is going to send me the details of the officer investigating from the Met, and I have contacted them already in relation to trial next year. I'm just making sure they have considered an intermediary if necessary for her and of course arranging an interpreter.   
I explained that at the moment we wouldn't be doing the video interview with her because of the risk it poses to her mental health. She was upset by this as she feels she will still have the same trauma, flashbacks, nightmares and thoughts regardless of if she does the video interview. I explained that every time we tried arranging a visit for doing it this is triggered a significant mental health episode. I told her that we will all stay in contact and if/when her mental health improves to a point that it will not risk significant harm to her then we will reassess and do it.
I've also told her that I will be speaking to my contact over in Romania and passing the Romanian Police everything that she has told us, that it is likely they will take the investigation. Also that I will try and establish what happened when she went over last time as she is alleged mistreatment by the Romanian police.
I let the staff member know, who is there but not part of the conversation, that we had told something that Claudia would be disappointed with and that she had become upset by this. However, when we left, she was in good spirits.

He was going in and out of the premises, carrying a black backpack and pulling a small suitcase, which suggested he was feeling unsettled. Staff approached him and prompted him to prepare a meal and take a shower, but MB appeared confused and unstable, which prevented him from following through with these tasks. He spoke about his past, specifically how his mother's behaviour had impacted his mental state when he was young. Despite this, he did not express further distress. Later in the shift, staff again prompted MB to cook and take a shower, but he declined both suggestions. fields.subject: Update from St Peter's Hospital assessment
fields.entry:
I have just assessed Matthew . This was my documentation. I have added all professionals entries from this email thread to his  medical record to demonstarte efforts of professionals ...

Consent gained to assess
CIWA 4 on tremor. last alcohol, yesterday at 4pm approx.
Attended with self harm to right forearm and eye injury.
Reports drinking 2x ltrs vodka most days. Every few weeks has to consecutive days not drinking any alcohol. He experiences alcohol withdrawal but no seizures. Advised sudden cessation  is dangerous and may lead to DT's or seizures.

Trigger: Matthew drinks alcohol when he feels his world is in chaos. When he lived in Guildford he drank only in the evenings , attended iaccess appointments, woodwork and did some gardening.
Since a forced move to Addlestone he can not afford to go to wood work which is £13 on the train approx and he is refunded £4. He has stopped gardening and finds it difficult to engage with iaccess and probationDNA yesterday 12.30iaccess appointment as attended at the wrong time. He reports that the appointments are not joined up as professionals have previously agreed and it is freezing waiting for appointments on his bike. His alcohol has increased which has impacted his behaviour , he has become verbally aggressive and is now awaiting eviction. Matthew  understands his key worker Jo feels to unsafe to work with him alone. He feels that the lack of communiction with Jo over the phone has made him feel useless and unimportant, which has further impacted his alcohol misuse

Motivation: Matthew can clearly identify that less alcohol leads to less anxiety and aggression. He is keen to work with services and would like support from Jo. He has insight in to his drinking behaviours and wishes to avoid a return back to prison. He feelsthat while the eviction is pending he will have little control over his impulse to drink alcohol.

Goal: Matthew would like to move back to Guildford. He discusses that he  attended RSCH once while he lived in Guildford as he was drinking far less alcohol and engaging with services.
Matthew will stabilise his alcohol use
He will attend probation and iaccess appointments in Guildford  if they are arranged together. He does not want to switch to iaccess NW team.
He would like support with his eviction and finding suitable accommodation in Guildford.
Matthew is keen to find alternative occupation and has discussed a community gardening project with Jo- He is reluctant to start anything in the Addlestone area, He does not want to form further connections locally

Denies dependents , denies illicit drug use , smokes unknown quantity of cigarettes. Feels his relationship with his sister is positive.
LFTS NAD . agrees to OP fibroscan to assess liver health.
MH : feels well in ED , self harming when intoxicated to release his frustration. Denies suicidal ideation

PLAN

CIWA scoring , if above 9 for 20mg chlordiazepoxide if above 15 for 40mg chlordiazepoxide
IV Thiamine

fields.subject: Response from probation - Lewis
fields.entry:
Just in terms of Probation it is certainly the intent to coincide appointments with i-Access moving forward. That said this was attempted on Monday but MB failed to attend both I understand. Certainly for this week I have had to move his appointment to 19/03 @ 2:30pm at College House as he is subject to weekly reporting. If MB does not attend joined up appointments he is going to find he has to attend on different days. A failure to attend a Probation appointment on any given week is likely to result in breach proceedings.

 

In terms of his eviction the only action we can and have taken is to submit a Duty to Refer to Surrey Council. As discussed with MB previously he has to temper his expectations as given his history any rehousing exercise is going to be incredibly difficult.

fields.subject: Day Shift
fields.entry:
PS was reported to be sleeping at the start of the day. Staff knocked on his door at 09:00 am, reminded him of the meeting with his social worker-kathryn at 10:00 am, At 09:30 am, PS requested for his morning medications and staff observed him while taking them. PS collected 3 cans of foster beer and returned to his room. At 10:05 am, the social worker-Kathryn arrived and had a meeting with PS first before staff could join them. The following were agreed with PS and his social worker-Kathry during the meeting:
•	Walk within the community: PS is allowed to take a walk within the community alone and his expected to return to the house within 30 minutes to 1hr. If he did not return within the agreed time, staff are expected to call his phone or report to the police if not seen within the environment. 
•	Local shopping: PS is allowed to go on his own to shop at the local store (Homebargain etc) with the sum of £5 allowance (Cash only). If he needs more than £5, the team leader/manager must be informed. PS is expected to return with the receipt of the transactions as evidence, staff must keep record of it in the individual petty cash. 
•	Cooking: PS has agreed to cook once in a week, preferable Saturdays. Staff on duty are expected to support him by ensuring that other residents do not come into the kitchen area at the time his doing his cooking.
•	Visit to Dad/Pub: PS agreed to be visiting his dad in the house, however he said the issue of the pub was just a one-off issue as the staff of the pub mentioned that they are having bookings for the day. PS mentioned that he didn't run away as staff later came to meet him and left the place together.
•	Recovery Activities: PS declined to visit the Lighthouse at Woking has suggested by staff and seconded by his social worker during the meeting.
At 02:00pm, PS had a meeting with his advocate and all went well. PS was well settled during the day; he appeared to be calm in his mood. At 18:40 pm, he requested for his evening medications, and he was observed while taking them. Staff gave him 3 cans of foster beer. PS remained in his room at the time of writing this note (19:06pm).

fields.subject: PH day notes
fields.entry: PH began the day having already taken his medication and presented as calm and settled, though occasional self-talk was noted. At 11:50 AM, PH left Johnstone House, dressed in black joggers and a black hoodie. An attempt by the house manager to support PH in withdrawing funds from his bank account at the cash point was unsuccessful due to a declined transaction. Subsequently, PH’s scheduled appointment with the community mental health team was cancelled. At 12:30 PM, day staff assisted PH in contacting his bank to resolve the banking issue. During the call, PH requested an address change, but the bank advised him that a physical visit was required for both address changes and fund access. Consequently, at 1:10 PM, the house manager escorted PH to Barclays Bank. By 2:10 PM, they returned to Johnstone House, having successfully withdrawn £300 and updated PH’s address at the bank. PH was then supported with his food shopping. At 3:40 PM, staff accompanied PH to his blood test appointment and to collect his medication at the Redwood Centre, Farnham Road Hospital. Following the blood test, PH became highly emotional, crying and remaining distressed until his return to Johnstone House, where he went directly to his room, despite attempts by the deputy manager to engage him. At 5:30 PM, PH requested and received £5 from his personal funds, signing for it before leaving and returning 20 minutes later. Staff assisted PH in reheating his pizza at 6:10 PM, which he then took to his room to eat. Finally, at 6:30 PM, staff supported PH with his evening medication. At 7.30pm PH lost his tobacco and he asked for more money to go buy some more. Staff gave him the money, he signed for it and left Johnstone house.

fields.subject: MS day notes
fields.entry:
MS was asleep at the start of the day shift, having gone to bed in the early hours. He awoke at 09:15 and showered, reporting to staff that he felt tired despite appearing settled and in a pleasant mood. At 11:15, Basil Kanusoko from the Mental Health Home Treatment Team contacted the house to advise he would be assessing MS. He stated he would arrange a psychiatric appointment to review MS's medication and potentially prescribe Clonazepam. MS became unsettled in the afternoon, reporting auditory hallucinations. Staff attempted to calm and reassure him, encouraging him to seek support from staff when feeling anxious. Throughout the afternoon, he was heard shouting angrily and using profanity. 

During the day, MS disclosed that witnessing the arrest of a former associate triggered his anxiety and fear. He also exhibited behaviours indicative of paranoia, purchasing newspapers daily to decipher perceived coded messages using mathematical formulas. 

At 18:00, MS returned to the house and immediately went to his room, subsequently experiencing a significant episode of auditory hallucinations involving interactions, specifically a confrontation, with figures from the Narnia chronicles and perceived demons. Following this episode, the house manager was consulted, who advised contacting the Crisis Team. They directed contact to the Home Treatment Team. Community RMN, Basil, visited the house and assessed MS, concluding a high risk of escalation. He advised that should MS's condition deteriorate, posing a risk to himself or others, emergency services were to be contacted for transport to A&E for psychiatric assessment and potential emergency medication. Currently, MS remains cooperative and pleasant during interactions with staff and residents, acknowledging his mental health difficulties. 

Basil has requested an urgent medical review for MS to assess and prescribe medication for his agitation and hallucinations. The house is awaiting confirmation of this appointment.

fields.subject: MS day notes
fields.entry:
At the start of the day shift, MS was already up and had started shouting and talking to himself. Day shift staff went up to him to check on his welfare and found him brushing his teeth in the bathroom. They exchanged greetings, and he informed staff that he had slept very well but was hearing noises now – night staff had reported that he was very quiet and slept through the night. At 8:20 am, staff supported him with his morning medication, after which he went out to the shops to get breakfast. He appeared unsettled but was calm and engaging when spoken to, although he was aware that he was hearing noises and voices. 
At 11:30 am, MS asked when the Home Treatment Team would be coming to see him, and staff informed him that they had referred him to a doctor to prescribe new medication to calm him down. MS’s hallucinations continued throughout the morning, especially while in his room alone. He continued to shout and swear in his room, threatening to fight and ‘sort out’ something or someone, and sharing how he was having spiritual encounters in his room. 
Out of concern for him and following the advice of the Home Treatment Team the day before, staff called emergency services at 1:00 pm. The call handler asked to speak to him and asked MS some questions, for example, if he was thinking of harming himself or others, or if he had lost any blood. He answered, stating that he is not a danger to himself or others and would not be capable of harming himself. The call handler then advised staff to call the Crisis Team instead and said they would be referring MS to the GP to assess him instead. 
At 13:40, the Home Treatment Team called and asked MS to attend a medical review at Gatton Place, Redhill, which he agreed to, and left on time to attend his appointment. At 15:00, MS’s mother called to check on his welfare, as he had earlier called his father and told him an ambulance had been called, and he was going to be taken somewhere. She was informed that he had gone to the Home Treatment Team for an assessment. At 15:10, MS returned from the Home Treatment Team and informed staff that they had agreed to prescribe him new medication. 
At 15:15, MS spoke to JN and said he was suicidal and had borderline personality disorder, advising JN to speak to staff if he was concerned about his safety. At 16:00, MS confronted JB for smoking weed outside the house, which JB denied. MS then told JB that he was pissing him off and that he should be mindful and keep away from him as he's not in a good mental state at the moment. When he was talking to JB, he asked that staff be there because he "needed them to be there". 
At 18:10, MS approached staff and informed them that he was hearing noises and sounds again. He needed reassurance and someone to listen to him, so staff talked to him and calmed him down. He was also given the number to the Crisis Team and encouraged to call and speak to them. After the conversation, MS came down and prepared his dinner.

fields.subject: JN day notes
fields.entry:
At the beginning of the day shift, JN was already awake. Staff attended to him promptly, assisting with his morning medication and checking his blood sugar level, which was recorded at 6.8.
At 9:20am, staff contacted Townsend Pharmacy to enquire about the delivery of JN’s weekly medication. The pharmacy explained they were unable to send out a new blister pack at this stage, as JN had recently been admitted to hospital. They were awaiting confirmation of any changes to his medication from Greystone Surgery before proceeding.
At 9:30am, staff followed up with Greystone Surgery regarding JN’s prescription. The call was passed on to the Prescriptions Team for further action.
Later, Dinesh from Greystone House Surgery phoned to confirm that JN’s prescription had been updated, and a new script had been sent to Townsend Pharmacy. He also arranged a medication review appointment for JN and advised that details would be shared with us in due course. Dinesh further informed us that JN has been taken off hydrocortisone until after his medical review and blood tests. He also made an appointment with the GP for them to review JN’s medication. 
As it was a sunny day, JN chose to go for a walk around the market. He returned approximately an hour later.
At 2:30pm, staff supported JN with his afternoon medication, after which he chose to rest.
At 6:00pm, staff assisted JN with his evening medication and another blood sugar check, which showed a reading of 7.0. At this point JN complained about the excess noise in the house which is preventing him from resting during the day.

fields.subject: MS day notes
fields.entry:
MS woke up just before 9:00am and went to the bathroom to wash his face and brush his teeth. He then came downstairs and informed staff that he was going out briefly but would return shortly to take his morning medication.
Staff supported MS with his morning medication without any issues.
Toyin from the Mental Health Home Treatment Team called to inform staff that he would be visiting MS at 12:00 midday.
At 12:20pm, MS's mental health care was formally transferred from the Home Treatment Team to the CMHRS Tandridge. The service will be transferred again to the Reigate Team next week. Two staff members from each team attended the property to facilitate the handover.
Throughout the morning, MS appeared settled and in good spirits. However, he was occasionally heard shouting loudly to himself from his room.
At 4:00pm, MS returned to the house after being out for approximately an hour. On arrival, he told staff that he had seen God outside and began a disjointed and erratic conversation about being chosen to establish the royal animal kingdom, although he expressed uncertainty about how to begin. Despite the unusual content of the conversation, MS remained calm and presented as reasonable throughout.
Further interactions with MS during the day revealed that he has been reading material on magic, druidism, folklore, spirituality, and the Bible, and appears to be interpreting these themes as reflections of his own lived experience.

MS was already awake and out of the house at the start of the day shift. He returned shortly after 8:00 am, wearing a black hoodie and black combat trousers which were covered in dry grass. He explained that he had been lying under a tree in the park.
Although calm and pleasant with staff, he appeared unsettled and was repeatedly going in and out of the house between 8:00 am and 9:00 am. He continued this pattern throughout the morning.
During interactions with staff, MS appeared to still be upset and unsettled following an altercation with local youths a few days ago. Each time he returned to the house, the back of his clothes suggested he had been lying on the ground or in grassy areas. While his conversations were less disjointed and erratic compared to previous days, he remained visibly agitated and distressed.
At approximately 1:00 pm, MS prepared lunch in the kitchen, then went to his room to rest. At 2:00 pm, Toyin from the Mental Health Home Treatment Team (HTT) called to speak with MS regarding the collection of his medication. As he was still asleep, staff made a note to remind him once he woke up.
MS woke up from his nap at around 3:30 pm. He was reminded to collect his medication from Gatton Place Mental Health HTT, and he complied.
In the evening, MS appeared settled. He played chess with JB and later watched TV with JN.

fields.subject: PH day notes
fields.entry:
PH was calm and settled at the start of the day shift, and staff supported him with his medication. Mid-morning, PH informed staff that he was unable to use his bank card. The house manager went to the cashpoint and shop to support him to withdraw money; however, the card failed again. Because PH had no money or food, the house manager used her own money (£30.70) to purchase two pizzas, milk, and tobacco for him. He stated he would repay this when the card issue was resolved.
At 14:00, staff called Barclays Bank to support PH in resolving the card problem. He was unable to fully identify himself; however, the bank staff informed staff that the card had been cancelled because it was reported lost on 8 April. They advised that he be escorted to the bank to order a new one and to withdraw money. They also advised that staff speak to his branch so a note is made on his account regarding making it easier for him to access his account because of his mental health illness. 
When PH understood what had happened, he became visibly upset and angry with himself, shouting and walked out of the house. PH returned 10 minutes later, and staff explained what had happened, at which point he was calm. He gave the cancelled bank card to staff, and it has been stored in the petty cash box. At 16:00, PH started to become agitated and unsettled, with his talking becoming increasingly loud. At 16:30, he was very agitated, loudly shouting expletives while walking in and out of the house. Staff then administered his PRN medication. Due to PH’s agitation and loudness, NF came out of his room at one point and asked him to calm down. By 17:30, PH had calmed down and was more settled, and he spoke to staff about his bank card.

At 18:00, staff prompted PH to take his evening dose of Clozapine, but he declined, stating he didn’t need it and that it was poison.

At the point of writing, he was asleep in his room.

fields.subject: PH day notes
fields.entry:
At the start of the day shift handover, it was reported that PH had gone to bed at 8:30 am the previous night and woken up at 6:00 am. He then went into the garden and began shouting expletives. Night staff asked him to quieten down as the neighbours were still sleeping, and he complied. He was sitting in the garden at that point, then he started pacing in and around the house, going in and out. At 8:10 am, staff prompted him to take his medication several times. He ignored them until five minutes later when he took the medication in his hand. Staff walked around the house and checked the ground to ensure he had not thrown the tablet away. Throughout this time, while staff were trying to talk to him, he was not responding, just silently pacing around the house and going in and out.
At 8:25 am, he walked out of the house, and staff monitored him from a distance to ensure he did not approach the neighbours. He returned at 8:50 am and sat in the garden.
During the morning, he could be heard talking to himself, but not shouting, and going in and out of the house. However, he seemed settled and calm.
At 10:20 am, PH asked for £10. As there was no ten-pound note available, staff gave him £20 and asked him to get a receipt. He then went out and returned with a new pack of tobacco. Staff reminded him that he already had tobacco in the house. At 11:50 am, PH asked for more money, stating he wanted to buy food. Staff reminded him that he had food in the fridge, but he refused it, saying he wanted to buy different food and that he would eat the food in the fridge later.
PH was calm and settled for most of the morning, but his talking to himself became louder in the early afternoon. When he was in the garden, staff asked him to keep his voice down.
At 3:45 pm (15:45), PH told staff that he was going out and has been quiet since his return.
At 6:00 pm (18:00), the member of staff supported PH with his evening medication, which he took without any issues.
PH only ate yoghurt the entire day – approximately six small pots. Staff offered to make him pizza, but he declined.
