fields.subject: PH day notes
fields.entry:
At the beginning of the shift, PH was already awake, having risen at approximately 06:00 following a full night’s sleep. According to the night shift handover, he attempted to access the garden upon waking but was redirected to the front of the property by night staff to minimise noise and avoid disturbing neighbours while smoking.

During the morning, PH appeared calm and settled, though he was noted to be quietly muttering to himself. At 11:45, staff offered assistance with meal preparation, which he declined, stating he intended to eat a pie from the refrigerator later. He engaged in a coherent conversation, during which he asked staff whether they perceived him as a human being and how he might be seen as one. He then sat quietly in the garden before returning briefly to the communal area and leaving the property at approximately 12:55.

By 15:00, with PH having been absent for around two hours, staff informed both the house manager and the on-call manager. It was advised that no immediate action be taken, as it was possible PH had travelled to Guildford.
At 17:15, staff contacted Guildford Police Station to check if PH had been located. Police advised staff to report him as a missing person via 101, and a reference number was provided: 047705052025. Staff also contacted the Royal Surrey County Hospital, who confirmed PH had not been admitted.

As of the time of writing, PH has not returned to the property.

fields.subject: Placement review with social worker (Stuart)
fields.entry:
The following is what we discussed in RB’s review meeting and also RB's input.
Settling In:
Explained to Stuart that RB has settled in well at Pinewood. He is interacting positively with staff and other residents and sometimes joins others to watch TV in the lounge.
He is allowing staff to support him with cleaning his bedroom and changing his bedding.
Ongoing Challenge: RB continues to resist changing his jumper.
Food and Nutrition
RB is currently on a structured food routine: breakfast, snack, lunch, snack, and dinner, with drinks in between.
Staff are encouraging water intake and monitoring his food portions appropriately.
Medication
RB is still prescribed all medications; however, he is only taking Atorvastatin 20mg at night.
Stuart took photos of all medication and will discuss with the doctor before getting back to us.
When asked about his medication RB stated he is only willing to take the Atorvastatin and Paracetamol, declining the rest because they make him sick.
Receipts and Financial Documentation.
Stuart declined to take old receipts to Deddie.
I received an email from Deddie advising staff are to dispose of old receipts, and going forward, receipts are to be scanned and sent to Deddie at the end of each month.
RB’s Feedback
RB shared that he enjoyed the car journey to Pinewood and likes his bedroom and the quiet environment.
He expressed that he would like a lamp shade for the hanging bulb in his bedroom.
When Stuart asked if he still wants to move, RB stated he still wishes to move to a different residence due to sharing a bathroom. He understands this will take time and said he doesn't mind waiting.
When asked about changing his jumper, RB said he would do so once he gets a new blue jumper.
He requested a GP home visit to discuss foot surgery.
Actions Agreed:
Staff to book a GP appointment for RB, requesting a home.
Staff to scan and send monthly receipts to Deddie by the end of each month.
Staff to support RB in purchasing the following clothing items (preferably in blue):
1 Jumper, Cotton boxer shorts, Cotton shirt, Two cotton T-shirts
4.      4.Staff to support RB with registering at the local library and obtaining a library card.
5.      5.Lamp shade to be provided and fitted in RB’s bedroom on the hanging bulb.

Additionally, staff liaised with colleagues at Frimley regarding the MRI booking. Staff at Frimley confirmed the appointment arrangements with both staff and PRS and stated that a confirmation email will be sent as a reference for the upcoming scan. PRS appeared settled and reassured following the conversations with both the Hepatology Nurse and the additional clarification provided regarding his care plan. Staff supervised PRS to take his evening meds. PRS appeared settled in his mental state.

fields.subject: MB night note
fields.entry:
MB returned to the residence at 8:00 PM, marking the beginning of the night shift, after being absent for several days. Upon arrival, he greeted staff and disclosed that he had stolen a pair of shoes from TK Maxx. He also mentioned that he had sold his phone because he had ran out of money. MB appeared unsettled and exhibited erratic movements throughout the house.

During his time in the shower, which lasted over an hour, staff discovered that he had been smoking. He had opened the window wide in an effort to prevent the smoke from spreading to the rest of the house. Staff addressed the situation, reminding him that smoking indoors is prohibited under the terms of his tenancy and house rules. He had previously received a written warning for this issue. Given his prior warning, the matter will be escalated to senior management. MB later admitted to smoking cannabis in the bathroom and assured staff that he would not repeat the behaviour. His demeanour remained unsettled, his movements erratic, and his speech was notably fragmented and disjointed. He also spent more than 90 minutes in the bathroom showering until staff requested that he come out.

At 11:10 PM, MB left the house without informing staff of his destination. He was wearing white shorts, a black puffer jacket without a t-shirt, and black trainers. He carried a black backpack and a bumbag. MB returned at 11:45 PM, then left again at 12:30 AM, returning at 2:25 AM. Upon his return, he paced around the house, eventually spending another hour in the bathroom from 3:00 AM to 4:00 AM. Staff approached him and asked him to exit the bathroom, but he refused, stating that he was using the toilet. Staff detected the odour of smoke emanating from the bathroom, indicating that he had been smoking again.
MB remained awake in the house until 6:00 AM when he finally went to his room. As of 7:00 AM, he remains awake.

fields.subject: Communication from EO's visor officer
fields.entry:
Hi Hannah / all,

 

I visited EO today and spoke to him about his behaviour in the house and told him to go and purchase his own cigarettes if he cannot go without. We spoke about the flashpoint the other day with another resident resulting in police attendance and he has been told he should just go to his room is someone returns intoxicated.

We discussed his non-compliance with medication and he claimed the depot injections left him with a lack of motivation. He has been off of it for several weeks now and to be honest I would suggest he has less motivation to do things now than before. He seems uninterested in most things and there is an increase in his pornography use and activity online.

I have tried to explain my concerns and where I think he is heading and he has agreed to start taking his medication again. I left him about to go and speak to staff about taking his tablet….did he take it after I left?

He spoke about want to approach people and engaging with them in an aggressive manner and sending a message to a female threatening to get his sister on her. He has been told he is sailing close to the wind but he needs to take some responsibility.

 

If someone could let me know if he has taken his tablet and whether this continues. If he hasn’t I will call him and prompt him.  I would also encourage staff to report any issues that could be offence related and requiring police attendance by calling police (101 or 999 if appropriate).

 

If possible, could we have an update on his engagement at his appointment yesterday and whether he has a new appointment planned after a period of being on the new meds?

 

Many thanks,

 

Graham

fields.subject: MS night notes
fields.entry:
At the start of the shift, MS was out of the house. It was reported during handover that he had left at 1:00pm and had not returned. MS came back at 8:15pm, asked to use the staff phone, and then went out again. He was wearing a black woolly hat, black joggers, and a black hoodie. MS returned to the house at 10:30pm and went straight to his room. Staff later prompted him to take his medication, but he declined.

At 11:30pm, MS came downstairs looking unsettled. He began pacing around the kitchen and living area, which were both in darkness at the time. Staff checked on him and, on closer observation, he appeared intoxicated. There was blood on his fingers, likely from needle puncture wounds on his left arm. He appeared dehydrated, with very dry lips, and his general appearance was unkempt. When asked how he was, he entered into a rambling, disjointed, and erratic conversation. He spoke about how his family were horrible to him, blamed him for taking drugs, and claimed he had been brainwashed into becoming a woman, and other spiritual and fictional stories. He was crying throughout most of the conversation, expressing a desire for a peaceful life. Staff listened patiently, allowing him to express himself. This helped calm him, and they encouraged him to look ahead to the next day, offering hope and new experiences. He listened and returned to his room at midnight. He was later heard singing softly to himself.

At 12:20am, MS came back downstairs and told staff he was hungry and didn’t have any food. He asked if he could go to McDonald’s to get something to eat. He returned 30 minutes later with food, which he took to his room. MS came downstairs again to get a glass of water, then went back to his room at 1:15am.

At 3:45am MS was still awake and he briefly came downstairs, said hello to LC who was in the living room, and then went back to his room.

fields.subject: S117 meeting on 20/05/2025 outcome
fields.entry:
Attended by:
Sheila - commissioner (Funding)
Dr. Christi
Conner - social worker
The S117 meeting focused on the ongoing challenges LC is facing, particularly in light of recent updates from Seacole and LC's expressed wish to move on.
Mental Health:
LC was asked about his current mental state. He shared that his mental health has been fluctuating; however, he has not self-harmed in recent months. While he acknowledged having thoughts of self-harm, he stated that he uses music as a distraction to manage these thoughts.
Medication:
When asked why he does not return for his medication while on social leave, LC explained that he believes he can manage for a few days without it. He added that this should no longer be an issue, as he has ended his relationship with his girlfriend.
Financial Concerns:
LC stated that he has not been paying his utility bills due to financial difficulties. While the option of setting up a standing order was discussed, LC was not ready to engage with this at the time. The social worker advised that he would revisit this during his next visit on 06/06/2025 at Holland House.
In preparation for that discussion, the social worker has requested a detailed breakdown of LC’s utility bills and arrears to gain a clearer understanding of the financial situation. An email has been sent to Junior to request this information.
LC was reminded that addressing this issue is important, as it may impact his eligibility for moving into lower-support accommodation.

fields.subject: Missing £3.50p notice to Social woker
fields.entry:
Hi Kathryn,

Below is a summary of the incident of false allegation by PRS that occurred today (report attached).

At 12 noon, staff entered PRS to call NHS-111 concerning his complaining that he was feeling feverish, after the NHS representative ended their conversation with him, staff ( Temi and Saheda) supported him to clean his room, took some his clothes to wash in the laundry machine, we arranged the coins found on the floor into the bed side drawer for him and left while he was on the bed trying to sleep.  At 14:50 pm, he came out of his room and approached staff (Temi) that he left £3.50p in his jacket and he cannot find it. PRS mentioned that either of the staff took it, whereas the jacket was picked from the floor and hanged in his wardrobe at the time we left the room after cleaning his room. PRS falsely accused staff of taking his £3.50p, he demanded that he want it back and he said he doesn’t want staff cleaning his room again.
 
Actions:
Staff followed PRS into his room searched his jackets and no coins was found in any of the jacket.
Staff showed PRS all the coins that was picked on the floor and placed in his bedside drawer.
Staff also showed PRS their pockets to ascertain that they don’t have any money on them.

We hope to discussed further on your next visit by Tuesday (27/05/2025)
Thank you.

fields.subject: JB's six weeks placement review
fields.entry:
Attended by
Ruth - Social Worker
JB - Resident
Sarah - JB's Mum
Juliet - Staff

The meeting started with positive feedback particularly regarding the support JB has received during periods of anxiety around to MS.
General Wellbeing:
JB has settled in well at Redhill. He is sleeping consistently, appears well-kempt, and maintains a clean-living environment. His personal hygiene has significantly improved—previously bathing once a week, he now bathes every other day and completes his laundry in line with his set timetable.
Medication:
He is consistently taking his night medication - quetiapine 25mg ; however, Lisdexamfetamine 50mg tablets. Is still pending due to Boots stating the prescription had a business rather than a hospital one. 
Mum is going to go to Epsom hospital to find out further information, she will let us know of the outcome.  
Substance Use:
JB has not used drugs since moving to Redhill however there was a time when he was drinking alcohol. This was met with his mother reducing his daily allowance from £18 to £4. Now his alcohol intake has decreased, there are concerns that he may be obtaining beer from someone else, as he is occasionally observed to be tipsy, though not fully intoxicated. JB has acknowledged that he does drink, but not daily—typically two or three cans of beer when he does.
Activities and Support:
JB has a pending telephone assessment with I-Access.
We are still awaiting responses from both Surrey Choices and Richmond Fellowship regarding.
Housing:
JB’s mother left two forms that need to be completed by the landlord and submitted to Reigate and Banstead Council. It has been agreed that she will return with the forms next week, and once signed, staff will deliver them directly to the council to ensure timely and secure.

fields.subject: EO
fields.entry:
EO:
EO was reported asleep at the start of the shift. He woke up at approximately 08:30 AM, approached staff to request his medication, which he took, and then returned to his room.

During the day, EO had a visit from his new care coordinator. They had an in-depth discussion focusing on EO's goals, plans, motivation, overall wellbeing, and medication adherence. EO was engaged throughout the meeting. The care coordinator explained the importance of taking medication regularly. At one point, EO became emotional and sobbed; he was given space to settle in his room before returning to continue the conversation. It was agreed that EO and his care coordinator will meet every two weeks. The care coordinator also spoke with staff to gain insight into EO's medication compliance. EO had shared that not taking his medication affects his motivation, noting that while he aspires to apply for jobs, he struggles with motivation despite available referrals. He also acknowledged recent boundary-pushing behaviours and expressed apologies to his care coordinator. EO discussed his smoking habits, expressing a desire to quit. He shared that he has implemented a strategy where he gives his cigarettes to staff, taking only one cigarette every three hours. This approach has helped him reduce his smoking to six cigarettes a day. Later in the day, EO shaved his hair, took a shower, and went out to town at 1:00 PM, wearing black trousers and a grey shirt with black accents. He returned at approximately 4:00 PM, appeared calm, and spent time in his room. He prepared dinner at 6:00 PM. Notably, EO did not smoke at all today.

fields.subject: JB
fields.entry:
JB
JB was reported to have left the premises around 18:00 pm when staff arrival on night shift. At 21:00 PM, staff attempted to contact JB to check on his wellbeing, but his phone appeared to be switched off. JB returned to the house at 22:21 PM and appeared to be heavily intoxicated. He went into the garden with MB, where they were engaging in loud conversation and shouting. Staff approached JB and asked him to lower his voice due to the noise, but he responded by shouting at staff. Other residents also asked JB to calm down, noting his level of intoxication, but he refused and continued to swear at staff.
When staff checked JB’s medication cupboard, they found it open and empty. JB stated that the night staff had removed his medication, but staff were unable to locate it. While observing JB, staff noted signs of heavy intoxication and contacted the on-call manager for further advice. JB later sat in the common area with LC and MS, continuing to swear at staff during this time.
JB insisted that staff give him his medication; however, staff were unable to locate the medication and could not administer it due to his level of intoxication. JB became verbally aggressive and called a staff member a 'stupid bitch. 
JB messaged his mother stating that staff were not giving him his medication. His mother then called the house phone and asked staff whether JB was intoxicated. Staff confirmed that JB appeared to be intoxicated, and his mother agreed that medication should not be administered under those circumstances. JB continued to deny consuming alcohol during the day, despite staff being able to smell alcohol on him. He also attempted to involve LC by asking him to support the false claim to his mother that he had not been drinking. JB accused staff of contacting his mother to say he was intoxicated; however, it was JB who initially messaged his mother. JB went into the garden and was observed shouting while speaking on the phone with his mother. JB then went upstairs to his room at 23:03 pm, where he was heard banging doors and shouting at staff. JB was shouting, which resulted in waking a resident who had been asleep. Staff attempted to ask JB to lower his voice, but he did not respond and continued shouting while in his room. JB fell asleep in his room at 00:30 am and remained there for the rest of the night. He appeared mentally unsettled and emotionally unstable at the time of writing this note JB is currently asleep in his room.

fields.subject: MS
fields.entry:
was asleep when staff arrived for the start of the shift. Staff then knocked on his door and asked him if he wanted to take his medication and he refused. Heather Tucker from Homefirst came to visit MS and speak with him but he didn’t want to talk with her. He then woke up and went out into the community. He arrived back an hour later mentally unstable requesting to get sectioned as he feels he wants to harm someone and himself. during this time staff contacted Heather from Home first and her colleague who attended the premises in the morning to see MS who declined to talk to them. While another staff was contacting crisis team for support who advised that due to the nature of threats staff to contact police for support. PC Jake and his colleague attended the premises around 12:50pm and supported MS to East Surrey Hospital for mental health assessment, they also requested for staff to go with MS. Police ref: 37728. 
Staff assisted MS to the hospital with the police. When staff and MS arrived at the hospital, we sat in the waiting area with the police but MS and one of the police kept going out because he was agitated. We waited for around 2 hours for triage to see him then Nurse Cruiz saw him with the police still with him. He explained to her that he wants to go back to hospital as he is hearing voices to harm others and himself. He told her that he had taken drugs 3 days ago (cocaine) with the intention of killing himself. He said he spent £500 worth. He was passed on to a psychiatric nurse who took him to a room to speak and assess him. She asked him questions like when was the last time, he took drugs and she stated that she can’t stop him from going out and harming himself the choice is his. He started shouting at her saying that he needs to be sectioned, and that the NHS don’t care and that he’s been in that position before that’s why he ends up leaving. He started slashing at his wrists saying, “I have to cut myself for you guys to take me seriously”. He threw a chair at the wall then the nurse left the room to get security, and they arrived and told him to calm down. the security stated to him that this is not the first time they’ve met and MS said “are you going to hit me, I’ll hit you back if you touch me”.  He then stated that he didn’t want to see that nurse again or he was going to hurt her. Staff spoke with her outside the room, and she stated that they are going to keep him, but they can’t be sure that he won’t just get up and leave the next day as it voluntary. Staff then left him with Mohammed from the psychiatric team who he’d met before.

fields.subject: MB
fields.entry:
MB
MB was seated comfortably in the communal area rolling a cigarette when staff arrived for the night shift. Staff observed that MB was smoking in the communal area and promptly reminded him that smoking is not permitted inside the house. MB then went outside to the garden to continue smoking.
Afterwards, MB returned indoors and went to his room. Shortly after, staff noticed that MB was smoking in his room. He was called out by staff and reminded again of the no-smoking policy. MB stated he needed to use the bathroom but was then observed attempting to smoke again in the bathroom. MB then left the bathroom and went downstairs to the kitchen, where he was observed making a cup of tea.
  MB returned downstairs and sat quietly in the common area for a period of time. He then went outside into the garden, where he was observed pacing around in circles with a backpack on his back. 

MB returned to the common area and was observed sitting in the dark, appearing to have some quiet time. Staff approached him to check on his wellbeing and offered to turn the light on. MB responded that he was okay and was just resting. Staff approached MB to check the contents of his backpack, as he had been observed repeatedly hiding it from staff view. Upon checking, staff found that MB had two large Galaxy chocolate bars, two large KitKat chocolate bars, and two large Cadbury chocolate bars. When asked where he had obtained the items, MB stated that someone had given them to him.
MB remained engaged in conversation with staff during the interaction. He expressed feeling bored and shared that he would like to go to a car boot sale, visit a farm, and even go to the beach. Additionally, MB mentioned an interest in planting in the garden, saying he enjoys flowers. MB went to bed at 00:51 and slept throughout the night. He appeared mentally stable and calm while in his room. At approximately 06:41, MB was observed exiting his room and leaving the premises without informing staff. At the time of leaving, he was wearing grey shorts, a brown long-sleeve top, and carrying a backpack on his back. As of the time of writing this note, MB has not yet returned to the premises.

 Regarding BQ’s absence from the property for approximately 24 hours, our protocol regarding BQ is as follows

fields.subject: PRS
fields.entry: PRS was reported to be in his room at the start of the shift. He had a mild altercation with ZGM because he opened the bathroom door on him without knocking. Staff immediately deescalated the situation and PRS went back to his room. He took his medication supervised then soon after he went to the garden for a smoke.  PRS returned 20 minutes later, and he went back to his room. At 14:40 while he was getting his beer, he stated to staff that he wanted to go around ZGM for he did not feel safe going past him. When ZGM overheard him saying this he became verbally aggressive towards Paul. While staff was supporting him to go around ZGM, the two would have an argument which staff intervened and stood in-between them to disengage. However, Paul continued to shout back and ZGM jumped over staff and slapped him.  Paul fell over and staff immediately supported him get up while protecting him from any more sudden attacks, but he would continue shouting back at ZGM. Staff and PRS would lock themselves in PRS room as ZGM continued to charge towards PRS.  Emergency services were contacted as when Pul was physically assaulted, he fell over and bruised his forehead. Pual declined speaking to the ambulance team stating that he did not require any medical attention, but he wanted the police to come and take ZGM, Ambulance reference number 3972. Police arrived at 15:33 and asked for PRS room, and they started assessing him. PRS informed police that this was not the first time that ZGM assaulted him since he moved. He continued to express that ZGM has been verbally aggressive with him and following him around asking for tobacco .PRS would even be heard making false allegation that ZGM had punched him three times meanwhile he was slapped once while staff stood between them to protect Paul. Police later came to staff and asked how the incident transpired. Staff gave the officer an outline on how the incident occurred and PC recorded it as a statement. Police reference SYP – 20250607-0529. When the police left staff supported by contacting 111 for advice following on PRS falling on the stair beam when ZGM assaulted him. Paul still declined to engage with them thus NHS clinical staff (Amal) advised staff to check on PRS every 6 hours to monitor any new symptoms. PRS continued, to be in his room and when staff checked on him twice, he was advising that he is alright. At 18:00 staff supported him with his evening medication and was observed while taking it.Staff prompted him to have something to eat, and he told staff that he will buy something later in the evening. At the writing of this report PRS was in his room and he appeared stable in his mental state and calm in his mood.

Resident ZGM was in the communal area at the beginning of the shift. During handover, it was reported that ZGM had sustained a finger laceration; however, the circumstances surrounding the injury are unknown. Staff asked him how his hand was and he said it was “okay”.

At 21:00, staff assisted ZGM with his night medication. When informed that his Zopiclone dosage had run out, ZGM reacted aggressively, questioning staff regarding the empty packaging. ZGM appeared to be in a calm and settled mental state in the presence of other residents, frequently going to the garden to smoke with them and sharing music selections on the television.

fields.subject: MB night note
fields.entry:
MB When staff arrival for the night shift, staff were informed that MB had been taken to the hospital earlier in the day for further checks.
At approximately 00:27, MB returned to the property and began banging on the front door. Upon entry, he appeared visibly distressed, agitated, and confused. MB informed staff that he could not recall what had happened to him prior to his return. He was slamming doors, disturbing other residents, and did not respond to staff's attempts to de-escalate the situation. Staff advised MB to try and get some rest.
Shortly after, MB asked staff for his backpack. He was advised to check his room, where he successfully located it. MB then went downstairs with the bag. A few minutes later, he returned upstairs and asked staff where his tobacco was. Staff advised him to check his bag again, as they were unsure of its location.
MB then proceeded to the communal area, where his behaviour escalated. He became increasingly aggressive and began causing significant damage, including:
•	Smashing the TV and DVD player
•	Damaging an electrical socket, which disrupted internet service
•	Spraying a fire extinguisher at staff and the everywhere in the house also force entry in PG room.
In response, staff immediately secured themselves in the office and called the police.
Following this, MB went to his room and continued to cause damage, including smashing furniture and breaking the window blind. He also damaged the garden door and several items in the garden, such as flowerpots and the clothesline. MB then exited the property.
Police arrived shortly thereafter. MB was seen fleeing the property and was later spotted again in the garden, but he ran off when approached by officers. Staff informed police of his whereabouts, but MB evaded capture.
As of the time of writing this note, MB remains at large. Police have advised staff to keep all doors locked, prioritise their safety, and to call 999 immediately if MB returns to the house.
Officer Herring 42288 confirmed that further details will be shared via email.
Ref 1606250018

PG was reported to be in his room when staff arrived for the night shift. At approximately 21:05, he came out of his room and went downstairs to collect a food delivery, which he took and then returned to his room.
At 11:15 PM, PG approached staff for his night medication. He took it without issue, but his mind was clearly elsewhere. He immediately brought up the terrifying events of the previous night involving MB, desperately asking if the police had arrested him. PG recounted how MB had tried to kick down his bedroom door, leaving him feeling utterly terrified and distressed. He said he “genuinely believed” MB was going to attack him and was insistent that MB be prosecuted for his actions.
PG was full of questions about MB's arrest, and staff advised him to wait for information they receive from the police to avoid misinforming him. They also suggested he raise his concerns with the deputy house manager upon their return. PG then voiced his fear: "Will MB be allowed to live here again?" He emphatically stated that he did not feel safe living here with MB. His fear and distress over the possibility of MB's return were palpable and emotional.
While he was supervised, he appeared mentally stable and calm in his mood. As of the time of writing this note, PG is currently asleep in his room.

MB then went outside to the garden, where he sat and smoked a cigarette. He later returned inside and sat quietly in the communal area. Throughout the night shift, MB appeared mentally stable but displayed signs of being unsettled in his mood, As I am writing report, MB is awake and present in the communal area.

fields.subject: Communication with Social worker 18.06.25
fields.entry:
Dear Hannah,
 I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to update you regarding BQ that occurred last night, and the subsequent actions taken by staff to ensure his safety and well-being.
At approximately 21:27hrs, BQ contacted staff and stated that he was going to kill himself. He requested that staff call his daughter. Following this, there was no further verbal communication from him, and the call was disconnected. Staff made several attempts to reach him by phone; initially, the calls rang through but went unanswered. Eventually, the phone stopped ringing entirely. The on-call manager was informed, and staff continued efforts to contact BQ.
 Staff sought consent from BQ to call an ambulance at least three times during this period, but he declined each time. BQ returned to the service at approximately 00:20hrs. At that time, staff noted visible swelling around the shin area of his leg and signs of compromised skin integrity around the shin area. He disclosed to staff that he had attempted suicide earlier and that he it’s been 3 days, and it has been crossing his mind. BQ would say they took everything from me and staff asked him who took everything from you when asked who "took everything from him," he declined to elaborate.
Despite staff encouragement, BQ declined support to prepare food. However, staff continued to offer emotional support, and he eventually appeared more settled, sharing pictures from his closet and laughing during the interaction. He also showed staff that he had taken his medication. Staff gently reminded BQ about the importance of his relationship with his daughter and asked why he would consider suicide, especially now that she had found him and was happy to reconnect. BQ apologised for the attempt and said he didn’t know what he had been thinking. He settled to sleep around 01:00hrs.
 
In response to this incident, the following actions have been taken:
 A referral was made to Good Samaritans for emotional crisis support.
 A GP appointment has been requested for today, though the surgery has yet to confirm the exact time.
Staff continue to monitor BQ closely and are offering both emotional and practical support.
 Kind regards,
Nichola

fields.subject: Appointment Mental Health review summary
fields.entry:
Update on BQ's Appointment with Mental Health Team – Dr. Keyshap and CPN
Dear all
Good day. Please find below a summary of BQ’s today appointment with the Mental Health Team, including Dr. Keyshap and the Community Psychiatric Nurse (CPN).
During the meeting, BQ was engaged in a discussion about his mental and emotional wellbeing. He expressed feelings of low mood and stated that he does not like himself. He disclosed a recent/ last week suicide attempt, where he tried to throw himself under a train in Woking. Fortunately, four men intervened and prevented him from doing so. He reported ongoing thoughts of self-harm and expressed a desire to be prescribed Morphine, Zopiclone, and beta-blockers with the intention of “sleeping forever.” BQ also shared that he missed yesterday GP appointment because he questioned the point of attending, expressing that he did not want to waste the GP’s time or his own.
BQ reflected on feelings of guilt when sober, particularly when people offer support. When asked about potential engagement with occupational therapy, he indicated a willingness, although he stated that nothing currently interests him. He also mentioned feelings of worthlessness and questioned why people want to help him, saying he feels undeserving of support.
Dr. Keyshap explored his alcohol use, and BQ acknowledged he drinks excessively to “escape from himself.” He reported currently consuming around six pints daily and wine. Despite his struggles, he shared that he still finds some solace in reading books, which he described as “brilliant” and a way to keep going. BQ identified his daughters as protective factors. He mentioned receiving a Father’s Day message from one of them, though he saw it a day late and found that the number had been blocked when he tried to reply.
Encouragingly, BQ expressed a desire to take a break from alcohol and has scheduled an appointment to meet with his Social Worker on Thursday, 26 June at 12:00 noon.
As part of his support plan:
 
·       Dr. Keyshap will engage the i-Access Team to explore prescribing Antabuse to help manage alcohol cravings.
·       BQ agreed to start on Mirtazapine 15mg, to be taken every evening under staff supervision. The medication will be held by staff and administered daily after 6:00 PM.
·       Dr. Keyshap personally collected the prescribed medication from the pharmacy and delivered it to staff.
·       BQ stated that he often says he is “fine” when asked, despite not feeling so, noting that he struggles to open fully. Dr. Keyshap reassured him that he has the team's full support and encouraged staff to reach out if any concerns arise.
·        Additionally, contact details for the Home Treatment Team were provided, should BQ wish to speak to someone over the weekends.
 Kind regards,
 Nichola

fields.subject: MB night note
fields.entry:
MB
Staff were informed that MB had left the property earlier in the day and had gone to the beach. Upon staff arrival for the night shift, MB returned to the house at approximately 21:32. He went straight to the bathroom, then proceeded to sit in the communal area, where he remained for most of the night. 
MB stated he was going for a shower. However, staff later knocked on the bathroom door to prompt him about the no-smoking policy, as there was concern, he may be smoking inside. MB initially insisted he was only having a shower, but it was then confirmed that he had been smoking in the bathroom. Staff reminded him that smoking indoors is not permitted and advised him to use the designated outdoor smoking area. At approximately 04:30 am this morning, MB refused to sleep in his room, stating that there was a spider present in his room. Staff conducted a check of the room and found no evidence of a spider. Following this, MB chose to leave his room and settled in the communal area, where he eventually fell asleep at 05:10am.
Staff later prompted MB to return to his room. Upon waking, MB appeared agitated and threw his pillows into the bin. Staff calmly prompted him to retrieve the pillows, which he did, and he then returned to his room.
MB appeared mentally stable but displayed signs of being unsettled in his mood. At the time of writing this note, MB is currently in the garden playing with water.

fields.subject: PRS

PRS returned to the house at approximately 21:45 and then went back to his room. PRS went to bed and slept through the night. He appeared mentally stable and calm in his mood. At the time of writing, PRS is currently asleep in his room.

fields.subject: Meeting with Social Worker - on utility arreas
fields.entry:
I just wanted to update you on my visit to Lee from today.

I discussed with Lee about the utility debt owed. Lee was hesitant to discuss this as was the case previously. I advocated for me to complete a referral to MH CAB. Lee was hesitant in relation to this but eventually agreed to for me to do this and someone from MH CAB to call him to discuss about the support they can offer to him. Lee said that he does not know knor does he want to know the amount he owed which I tried to discuss with him. Lee said that he is wanting to pay this debt but that he is not sure how to do this. I said that MH CAB would be able to support with this in addition to seeing if Lee is on the right amount and right benefits.

 

I discussed with Lee in his room has a clothes on the floor in bin bags in his room. Lee does not have storage space in his room. I discussed with Lee about seeking support from his supported accommodation to look at storage solutions. I followed up with discussing with the member of staff at the accommodation (tenaka).

 

I said to Lee that I am yet to hear back from Croydon in relation to supported accommodation in their area for Lee to be closer to his sister. I have chased this by emailing other professionals and teams and have not heard back currently. I said to Lee that I would chase this and let him know when I hear something back about this.

fields.subject: Meeting with Social Worker - Jennifer
fields.entry:
Jennifer is JRS's new social worker as Chris is on long sick leave. - we have updated his individual profile.
She came to discuss the issues regarding JRS’s failure to pay his utility bills. We reviewed all prior meetings involving Shemaine, Chris, and Sue from CAB, who has been supporting JRS with his PIP and ESA claims in an effort to increase his benefits.
I noted that communication between Redbridge and Seacole had been minimal until Chris and Seacole lawyers became involved, which marked a turning point in managing JRS’s rent payments. We also discussed efforts to obtain a bus pass for JRS, which were hindered due to limited communication from Redbridge.
All financial meetings between Chris and Redbridge were reviewed. She stated she had come to review the accumulated utility bills. I explained that these were intended to be paid from JRS’s benefits (PIP or UC). She inquired whether Redbridge was aware of this arrangement. I confirmed that invoices had been sent to Redbridge monthly, and we went through all correspondence as evidence.
I also addressed property damage caused by JRS. Redbridge has declined to hold JRS accountable for any of the damages incurred. She advised that while she cannot assist directly with the issue of damages, if the tenancy agreement states that residents are responsible for property damage, then Redbridge should acknowledge this responsibility.
During her visit, she requested to see JRS. However, he became agitated and shouted at her, claiming she was “useless like other social workers” who had not removed him from his appointee.
She left with all requested documentation and advised she would be meeting with her manager on Monday, 23/06/2025. She will provide an update following that meeting.

fields.subject: BQ Appointment - Communication
fields.entry:
Subject: Update on Home Visit – BQ

Dear all,

I am writing to provide an update following a home visit to BQ by the Home Treatment Team on Saturday as part of his follow-up support.

During the visit, BQ was engaged and communicative. He expressed ongoing frustration with his mental health difficulties, describing it as feeling like a "cycle." Despite these frustrations, he presented as settled and clearly stated that he has no intentions of harming himself. BQ reported that he has been taking his newly prescribed medication as directed and noted that he has not consumed alcohol since Thursday. This indicates a positive step in his engagement with treatment and self-care.

Kind regards,
Nichola

fields.subject: MB- SLEEPING ON THE GRASS OVERNIGHT
fields.entry:
Hi Sarah,

It has been noted that MB was seen sleeping on the grass with his bed sheet, pillows and duvet, I was informed the moved out of the house in the middle of the night and decided to sleep on the grass overnight, he had drinks and left over of foods lying beside him.
 
In the morning, when MB noticed that I have arrived at the premises, he left the place and went away from the premises.
 
Action:
 
Staff offered support to pack all the bed sheet, duvet and pillows that he placed on the grass back into his room.

When he returned to the house at 12:54pm, Staff had 1:1 key session with him, to inform him of the adverse effect of sleeping outside in the weather and the hazardous impact that it might have on his health.

Staff also cautioned him that he is creating an impression of being vulnerable and a threat to the neighbours by exposing himself outside overnight.

Staff made him aware that the neighbours are not comfortable with his act of sleeping outside on the garden grass overnight.
We will continue to redirect MB from this act and let you know if we have any further concern with his behaviour.

Thank you.

Temitope Fadipe

Team Leader.

fields.subject: Communication to BQ's social worker
fields.entry:
Dear  Hannah,
Good morning,i  hope this email finds you well. I am writing to provide an update regarding BQ’s behavior overnight. The night staff observed signs of acute emotional instability and intoxication. Below is the incident summary
Incident Summary:
BQ was not present when staff arrived. He returned to the premises at 22:43 and remained in the front yard, shouting and refusing to come inside. Staff discovered alcoholic beverages hidden in his bag, which were promptly disposed of. BQ appeared visibly intoxicated and repeatedly shouted, “I’m trying to wake the cunts up.”
Upon eventually entering the house, BQ lingered in the communal area, continuing to shout, throw objects, trying to cause property damage. He remained awake throughout the night, moving in and out of his room while using abusive language and attempting to break items.
At 07:30, BQ left the house again, wearing a black shirt and blue jeans. His behaviours continued to indicate emotional instability.
Actions Taken:
BQ was continuously monitored throughout the night.
Staff made repeated attempts to de-escalate the situation and negotiate with him, but he was unresponsive to intervention and left the premises.
Incident was logged in accordance with protocol.

fields.subject: MB
fields.entry:
MB:
MB was reported to awake at the start of the day shift. It was reported that MB complained that he does not have money, and he had damaged the kitchen waste bin. MB approached staff to reach out to his appointee to know why his bank card was not credited. Staff initiated a phone call and got no response; staff then sent an email to the appointee and copied the social worker. 
Incident 1 (MB FRUSTATION):
At 11:20 am, MB approached staff that he did not received money in his bank today as he has gone to check three (3) times. Staff persuaded him to go back and check again which he went. MB returned to the house shortly and said he there was no money. In his presence staff call the CFA-appointee phone number but the calls keep going to answering machine. MB left the office to the back garden and staff saw MB slamming the chairs on the floor and the house waste bin, staff persuaded him to stop, and he returned to the house. Afterward, MB went into the kitchen sprayed ketchup and salt all over the walls, floors and spread the dirt’s in the bin on the floor. Staff approached MB and he said his frustrated for going to the ATM more than three (3) times and his bank card is not funded. Staff offered £20 to buy tobacco, body wash and food that he claims he wanted. MB returned that he only bought tobacco worth £18.35 and kept back the change of £1.65p.
Incident 2 (MB MISUSED OF SUBSTANCE (Crystal and Ketamine):
At 13:15 pm, MB started screaming for help from the communal area and staff immediately approached him, he was hallucinating, staggering, jumping and slamming himself on the floor while shouting.
Staff tried to find out what happened, MB mentioned that he had taken substance -Ketamine and sniffed Crystal. Staff called the emergency service -999 (Ambulance) at 13:25, the team promised to send an ambulance while staff kept on engaging him. MB continued to hit himself on the floor, rolling on the floor and making attempts that he wants to fly. At 14:05 pm, staff called the emergency services -999 (Ambulance) again and they said once an Ambulance is available, they will reach the house address.
At 14:35pm, the Ambulance team arrived, they did his vital body sign check, had a conversation with him to know the substance he used. At 14:55, MB was taken away to the hospital.
MB nanny called the house phone at 14:15pm, that she had a conversation with Sarah Dee- social worker to get MB an Oyster card for transport and that she would like to have the bank account statement for MB to know what MB has been spending money on. Staff asked her to speak with social worker or the appointee for the account statement.
At the time of writing this note, MB is away at the St. Peter’s Hospital (19:08 pm).

fields.subject: BQ
fields.entry:
BQ was reported asleep at the beginning of the shift. He woke up at 12:45 PM and approached staff for his medication. He appeared agitated and accused staff of being inconsistent in administering his nighttime medication. This ongoing issue appears to be linked to BQ returning to the premises intoxicated, often after 12:00 AM. Due to these challenges, staff contacted BQ’s Care Coordinator for guidance. The Care Coordinator visited BQ on-site and confirmed that he had not slept the previous night and was visibly intoxicated during the meeting. BQ admitted to consuming approximately six cans of beer and a bottle of wine. He stated that Mirtazapine makes him feel good but continued to accuse staff of inconsistent support regarding its administration.
Following the visit, the Care Coordinator emailed BQ’s psychiatrist, Dr. Kayshap, who provided clear instructions: Mirtazapine must not be administered if BQ is heavily intoxicated. The Care Coordinator encouraged BQ to reduce his alcohol intake. However, BQ responded that he cannot stop drinking and expressed that he would prefer not to take the medication at all if it cannot be given consistently. Staff raised further concerns that BQ may not always fully disclose his alcohol intake, which could pose significant risks if medication is administered without full knowledge. Staff requested the Care Coordinator to continue consulting with Dr. Kayshap on how best to proceed in such cases. In the meantime, per Dr. Kayshap's guidance, staff will continue to document each instance when BQ misses his medication. At approximately 1:45 PM, resident BQ left the premises wearing a blue t-shirt, grey/green pants, black shoes, and a black sling bag. He returned at 6:41 PM, appearing slightly intoxicated, and inquired whether he would receive his medication that evening. Shortly after, BQ prepared a meal and proceeded to his room. While passing the communal area where another resident was watching television, he became agitated and verbally expressed frustration, stating that "people watch tennis all day long." In anger, he threw his plate of food and a fork at his room door. Moments later, BQ exited his room, took the TV remote control, and attempted to change the channel. He became further agitated, threw the remote to the ground, breaking it, and returned to his room. Residents emerged from their rooms, visibly distressed, and expressed that the ongoing disruptions were affecting their ability to sleep and feel safe. Reference number 0730- 3rd July2025

Actions Taken:
•	Staff immediately contacted emergency services due to escalating behaviour and resident concerns.
•	Police arrived promptly and engaged with staff to assess the situation.
•	Upon inspection, police found BQ in bed with broken plate fragments and food scattered across his room floor.
•	BQ informed both staff and police that he would not be taking his medication and continued to display signs of agitation.
•	Police warned BQ about disturbing the peace and advised him to respect the shared living environment. They made it clear that further breaches could lead to additional police involvement.
•	Police engaged the residents about the incident, and they expressed how they feel about his behaviour. 
•	With police present, staff cleaned the room, removing broken plate pieces and food debris.
•	BQ stated he would replace the broken plate.
•	Police advised staff to issue a formal written warning to BQ for breaching house rules and disturbing fellow residents.
•	At 7:51 PM, BQ exited his room again, still agitated, and told police he was going out and wouldn’t return. He was last seen in the garden area smoking and shouting as police departed the premises. He then went back to his room by 08:00pm and left again at 20:05 pm putting on a blue jean, blue t-shirt, carrying a black sling bag  and black shoes he mentioned that he is not coming back.

 Hi Karen,

Regards
Nichola

fields.subject: MB night note
fields.entry:
MB At the start of the night shift, MB was reported to be out in the community. He returned to the property at approximately 20:15 and went straight to the bathroom. Shortly afterward, staff observed MB shouting at another resident and making inappropriate and offensive remarks. MB then left the area and went to the communal area, where he lay down on the sofa and remains there for some time. 
During a conversation with staff, MB expressed concern about one of the residents who’s according to him, needs to have a wash. MB explained that he cannot use the kitchen because the resident’s strong body odour makes him feel sick.
Staff acknowledged MB’s concerns and reassured him that hygiene and communal space comfort are taken seriously. Staff advised MB that the issue would be addressed appropriately and monitored to maintain a respectful and clean environment for all residents.
At approximately 04:30 AM, MB woke up appearing visibly frustrated and began pulling down the curtains in the communal area. He then proceeded to the kitchen, where he began loudly banging and breaking kitchen utensils, including plates, cups, and a grater.
Staff also observed MB smoking in the communal area, which is against house rules. When prompted by staff to stop and reminded of the no-smoking policy, MB ignored the guidance and continued to smoke indoors.
Staff approached MB and calmly asked him to stop the disruptive behaviour and to pick up the rubbish he had previously left behind. MB continued shouting and screaming, becoming increasingly verbally aggressive. He stated, “I told you to open the f**ing door.”*
Due to the escalation and to maintain safety, staff opened the door to allow MB to leave the premises. MB exited the property at approximately 04:45 AM, wearing black trousers, carrying a black backpack, and with his T-shirt draped over his shoulder. At approximately 05:35 AM, MB returned to the property and proceeded to the communal area, where he lay down on the sofa. At the time of writing this note, MB appears mentally stable but remains visibly angry in his mood. he is currently asleep on the sofa.

fields.subject: communication of social worker to CMHRS
fields.entry:
I’m writing to raise concerns regarding Lee Chambers, following recent updates from his placement and my previous correspondence with Juliet on 9 July.

 

As shared earlier in the email chain, there have been ongoing issues with Lee’s mental health presentation, including medication refusal, disrupted sleep, and increased disengagement. I had noted that I would hold off on visiting until there was a more stable opportunity to engage with him meaningfully, and I requested updates on CMHRS involvement and any formal steps form placement in relation to refusal to address utility debts.

 

Since then, I’ve received a further update from the placement (11 July), reporting that Lee returned to the house intoxicated, attempted to bring a woman into his room, and was dismissive of staff reminders about house rules. He left the property at 23:00 and returned at 08:45 the next morning, having lost his phone and bank card. He continues to refuse medication and is reportedly not sleeping well.

 

Given the escalation in risk and deterioration in his presentation, I would like to advocate for support from the CMHRS with Lee directly to assess his current mental health needs and explore whether any additional support or intervention is appropriate at this stage. Your team’s involvement would be invaluable in helping to stabilise the situation and support Lee’s ongoing placement and future planning.

Please let me know if this is something that can be reviewed, and whether a joint visit or case discussion might be helpful.

 

Regards,

 

Connor Parrish
Mental Health Social Worker – South West Mental Health Social Care Team

fields.entry:
LC has an allocated clinician who reviewed him on the 7th of July, and he has a medical review booked for 18th July 2025.

 

Kind regards

Caroline

fields.incident_details: NP was in his room at 15:50pm, staff heard him talking on the phone and later he began to shout, and staff heard sound in his room. NP continued to shout, staff and LC rushed to his door and forced it open. NP was found sitting on the floor with broken plastic plate beside him and he could not stand up. Staff immediately called the emergency services as his speech was not coherent. NP shouted that staff should not call the ambulance as he refused to speak with the emergency services agent. He said staff should leave his room that he would be fine, but staff was guiding him not to fall. The emergency services promised to send ambulance and stated that it might take up to 4 hrs before their arrival. At 16:15pm, he came out of his room and said he found a substance at Addlestone bridge which he thought it was Cocaine, but it was Ketamine, and he used it. NP told staff that he needs to go out of the premises to get fresh air and he would be fine. At 16:20 pm, staff heard him calling a friend and he gave the postcode of the house to the person. Staff persuaded him to sit down and relax instead of going up and down the premises. At 16:33 pm, he left the house with Luke Clement into the community and NP told staff that he would be fine’’.

fields.subject: Day Note
fields.follow_up_notes:
PG:was reported to be in his room sleeping at the start  of day shift. PG woke up at around 10:45am and requested his medication from staff to which he was supervised while taking. Staff observed him to seem shaky and was very sweaty. Staff asked him if he was okay to which he said he was fine. At 11:15 he came running out of his room and told staff that he had been secretly drinking an excessive amount of alcohol to which he has now ran out of money and alcohol and is currently having withdrawals as he wasn't just meant to stop drinking straight away and go cold turkey, stating that it should of been a gradual process. He then went on to advise staff that he had contacted 111 to get advice about the current symptoms he was having ( Shaking and sweating) and they advised him to go to A&E at  Royal surrey hospital as it was an emergency and that his symptoms would progressively get worser and he was waiting for a taxi to get himself admitted stating he would potentially be back in a couple of days or longer. 

Staff asked PG if he knew what ward he was going to but he declined stating he would find out when he gets there and request for them to contact the house when they find out.  Shortly after getting dressed, he demanded to take all his medication stating he would bring it back when he was discharged.  

PG then proceeded to wait outside while staff engaged him in conversation and advised that they would be calling to check in on him and he also advised that he contact staff if they admitted him and the ward that he will be on. His Taxi arrived at 12:10 and he left on his way to the hospital. Staff called Royal surrey hospital at 14:26 and they confirmed that PG was at the hospital and was awaiting treatment and to be seen by a doctor.PG returned to the house at 17:40 and staff asked him how he was feeling, he told staff that he was feeling much better and gave staff his discharge summary. The doctor advised PG not to stop drinking abruptly as this can lead to withdrawal symptoms and was advised again to seek attention from i-access. At the writing of this report PG was in his room and he appeared fairly settled in his mental state.

We’ve been concerned about this resident’s behaviour previously over the past few days. He’s been outside our house quite often staring at the door, talking / shouting to himself and he’s often in the garden early most mornings doing the same thing. Today, when he tried to gain access to our home, it sounded like he was talking about “borrowing someone’s brain” for whoever he was talking to.  My partner has also heard him shouting several times, talking to himself in the street about how they ‘aren’t a human being’, amongst other things. It does appear he’s talking to a voice that he’s hearing. It appears to us that the situation and the resident’s behaviour is escalating.  We’re keen to be good neighbours and support you in your work wherever possible. We understand the service you’re providing and the resident’s needs. However, incidents like today aren’t acceptable and this made us feel unsafe in our home, so I just want to highlight how concerning this is for us.

fields.follow_up_notes: BQ – Absence from Premises and Intoxication Concern
fields.future_preventative_action: Review BQ’s current risk assessment and support plan.  Consider mental health and substance use support referrals.  Hold a keyworker meeting to discuss recent patterns of behaviour.
fields.action_taken: Staff attempted verbal de-escalation and encouraged BQ to remain indoors.  On-call manager was promptly informed.  Multiple phone call attempts were made to establish contact.  Police were notified and a missing person report was filed.  Full details were provided to attending officers.  BQ was supported upon return and monitored.  Incident reported for review and appropriate follow-up.
fields.incident_details: At the start of the day shift on 11/05/2025, BQ was seen in the backyard garden smoking. Staff greeted him and asked about his recent behaviour, including his prolonged time outside and suspected drinking. BQ responded, “I’m always a good person. At 08:05 AM, BQ returned to his room briefly to collect his sunglasses. He then left the premises at approximately 08:10 AM, wearing a beige half-zip knit sweater and army green shorts. Staff attempted to encourage BQ to remain indoors and rest, but he declined. Staff also advised him to take his phone so they could stay in touch and monitor his wellbeing. BQ ignored the advice and left the premises without his phone. The on-call manager was notified immediately. She advised that no action could be taken until 12 hours had passed, at which point BQ could be formally reported as missing. Attempts were made to contact BQ via phone at the following times: 10:20 AM – Phone rang, but not answered.12:50 PM, 14:00 PM, and 18:00 PM – Phone was switched off. At 18:00, the police were contacted, and a report was filed regarding BQ’s whereabouts. The reference number provided was 110520250673. When the night shift commenced, BQ was still absent from the premises. Police officers visited the property to inspect BQ’s room and collect further information. They advised that they follow up regularly to check for his return. At 04:48 AM on 12/05/2025, BQ was brought back to the premises by police, who reported finding him in Guildford. He appeared intoxicated and mentally unstable upon return. Staff supported him into the property, after which he went straight to bed. BQ remained in his room asleep for the remainder of the night shift.

fields.subject: BQ
fields.follow_up_notes: Since the incident on 29/05/2025, I’ve had time to reflect on what happened and how it affected me and the people supporting me.  I’ve spoken with staff at the residence about the situation, and I understand now why they were so concerned. I realise that being out for over 24 hours without letting anyone know was risky and caused a lot of worry.  I’ve agreed to wear my hearing aids more consistently, especially when I go outside, so I can better communicate and understand what's happening around me.  I’ve had a conversation with my social worker, who was updated about the incident. We discussed some of the reasons I left and ways I can ask for help next time instead of disappearing.  I’ve worked with staff to start putting together a personal safety plan. This will help me know what to do if I feel like I need space or am struggling to cope.
fields.future_preventative_action: I understand that what happened on 29th May was serious, and I recognise that it may put me at risk. I want to work on keeping myself safe and making better choices going forward. Here are the steps I agree to take (with support where needed) to prevent this from happening again:  Wearing My Hearing Aids Regularly: I will make sure to wear my hearing aids when I go out so I can understand people better and communicate in case of emergency.  I will inform staff before leaving the residence, and I will try to say where I’m going and when I expect to be back. I understand that this helps staff keep me safe and respond quickly if anything goes wrong.  I’m open to having regular check-ins by phone or in person when I’m out for long periods. This will help everyone know I’m okay and reduce worry. I’m willing to speak with staff, my social worker, or a support worker to talk about what led to me going missing and how I was feeling. This might help me understand my own actions better and get the right support for my mental and emotional well-being.  I know I need help looking after my health. I’ll try to attend medical appointments and stay in contact with professionals involved in my care. I’m willing to accept support with this. I agree to work with staff and my social worker to create a personal safety plan that can be used if I feel overwhelmed or want to leave the residence again. This plan will includes me calling a taxi when I’m intoxicated to get public transport.
fields.action_taken: Staff spoke with the police and gave them advice on how to communicate with me without my hearing aids.  They followed up with Royal London Hospital to check on my condition and location.  When I came back, the night staff observed me and made sure I was okay.  A safeguarding concern was raised because I had been missing and vulnerable, and there were signs I hadn’t been looking after myself properly.  My social worker was informed about the incident and the outcome.
fields.incident_details: On the 29th of May 2025, I didn’t return to the residence, and I was away for over 24 hours. I understand that staff became worried about me. At around 2:58 in the morning, someone found me lying on the ground near Tower Bridge in London. I had some visible injuries, and they called the police. When the police arrived, they checked on me and called an ambulance. I didn’t have my hearing aids with me, so I couldn’t properly hear what they were saying, and I couldn’t respond very well. I know this made things harder for everyone. The ambulance crew looked me over to see if I needed to go to hospital. While I was being assessed, the police contacted staff at Kingfield to update them. I’m told they also informed Surrey Police. Because I couldn’t hear properly, the officers asked staff how best to speak with me. Staff explained that they should talk clearly and loudly close to my ear, which helped a bit. A few minutes later, staff called the police again to ask for the incident number and a reference, but the officers didn’t have that information on hand at the time. The police told staff that I was being taken to Royal London Hospital in Whitechapel. They advised staff to ring the hospital after about half an hour for an update. At 4:37 AM, staff called the hospital, and they confirmed I had arrived there at 4:15 AM and was in A&E Zone D. No further details could be given at that point, and staff were asked to call again in the morning once I had been seen by medical staff. On the morning of the 30th of May, at 8:45 AM, hospital staff contacted Seacole and reported that I had left the hospital without being formally discharged. I know this probably caused more concern. Later that evening, at about 8:15 PM, I returned to the residence. The night staff said I seemed fairly settled. I wasn’t drunk or under the influence of anything. I made myself a meal and then went to bed without any issues.

fields.subject: Incident Involving BQ – Urgent Welfare Concern
fields.follow_up_notes: This morning, I woke up feeling emotionally drained but slightly more grounded than the night before. I was aware of how serious things had become, and I felt a mix of shame, confusion, and relief that I was still here. Staff checked in with me gently and asked how I was feeling. I told them I was still struggling, but I was grateful that they were there.  My leg was still swollen, and the skin around my shin looked a bit swollen. Staff encouraged me again to seek medical attention. This time, I agreed, and arrangements were made for me to be seen by a healthcare professional. I didn’t want to, but I knew it needed to happen.
fields.future_preventative_action: I will speak to staff or use my support contacts when I start to feel overwhelmed, rather than keeping things to myself until they escalate.  I will work with staff to create a personal safety plan, including steps I can take when I begin having suicidal thoughts and a list of people I can reach out to for support.
fields.action_taken: A referral was made to Good Samaritans for emotional crisis support.  A GP appointment has been requested for  18.06.25  at 14:15 Staff continue to monitor me closely and are offering both emotional and practical support.
fields.incident_details: 17.06.25 | Time: Approx. 21:27hrs  At around 21:27, I called staff and told them I was going to kill myself. I asked them to call my daughter. After that, I couldn’t bring myself to say anything else, and I hung up the call. They tried calling me back several times. At first, the phone rang, but I didn’t answer. After a while, I just stopped responding completely.  They asked me more than once—at least three times—if they could call an ambulance, but I refused each time. I didn’t want that kind of help then.  I returned to the service at around 00:20. My shin was swollen, and the skin around it didn’t look good. When staff asked me what had happened, I told them that I had attempted suicide earlier. I also admitted that these thoughts had been on my mind for the past three days. I remember saying, “They took everything from me,” but when they asked me who I meant, I didn’t want to talk about it.  They offered to help me prepare some food, but I said no. I wasn’t interested. Still, they stayed with me and supported me emotionally. After a while, I began to feel a bit calmer. I even showed them pictures from my closet, and we laughed together. I showed them that I’d taken my medication.  One of the staff gently reminded me how much my daughter means to me and asked why I would think about suicide—especially now that she had found me again and wanted to reconnect. That really made me think. I apologised and told them I didn’t know what I had been thinking. Eventually, I settled down and went to sleep around 01:00.

Reported that Brian has remain mentally stable with no evidence of alcohol use. Reported Brian travelling today to Portugal for holiday and will return on 27th March and has remain generally stable in mental health.

 His social worker (Hannah) said she has work with Brian for the past 3years this is the only time he has seen Brian being abstinence from alcohol for this period. Otherwise if it is omission it is important for GP to review his physical health.Dr Kashyap explained that his previous inpatient admission to Victoria ward they did not fin any evidence of depression or suicidal threat. fields.title: Incident
fields.issue:
I woke up at approximately 10:15 hrs, exchanged greetings with staff, and was supported in taking my medication. After that, I consumed some alcohol and returned to my room.

Later in the shift, staff approached me regarding a receipt for food I had purchased the previous day. I complied and brought the receipt to staff, explaining that I had already returned the change the day before. Staff then contacted the night staff for clarification, and they stated that I had not returned the £15.00 in change.

Upon hearing this (at approximately 15:00 hrs), I became visibly agitated. I raised my voice and shouted that the money was mine and that no one had control over it. I used inappropriate language, including swearing and calling staff “idiots.” Staff engaged with me calmly and reminded me to speak respectfully. I responded by saying that this was how I was used to communicating.

Staff then warned me that aggressive behaviour and the use of offensive language toward staff would not be tolerated and advised me that the police may be contacted if my behaviour escalated or became threatening. I said I would collect my beer and return to my room, which I did.

There were no further incidents, and I remained in my room for the rest of the shift.
fields.action_plan: Staff de-escalated the situation through calm, non-confrontational engagement. I was advised about acceptable behaviour and the consequences of continued aggression or verbal abuse, including the possibility of police involvement. The incident was recorded and escalated to management for further review. My keyworker will follow up with me to address communication strategies and to review expectations for respectful interaction with staff. Staff will continue to monitor me for any further behavioural concerns.

fields.title: Staying Safe When I Can’t Use the Bus
fields.issue:

I’m sociable, independent, and enjoy engaging with others in the community. I usually manage well and am open to practical solutions that support my independence. There may be times when I’ve had a drink or feel unwell and I’m unable to get the bus home. In these situations, I’ve agreed to use one of the taxi numbers I’ve saved on my phone to make my way back safely.
To support me with this:
•	I will use my own phone to call a trusted local taxi when I feel I can’t manage the bus.
•	I’ve agreed to give staff £40 to hold on to, specifically to pay for taxis in these situations.
•	When I arrive home by taxi, staff will support by paying the fare directly using the £40 I’ve already provided.
•	Staff will let me know how much was used and how much remains.

fields.title: Behavioural Concerns, Medication Compliance,
fields.issue:
Behavioural Concerns, Medication Compliance, and Re-engagement with Support (Update)Home appointment with my visor officer 20.05.25
I had a conversation with my Visor Officer about some of my behaviour in the house. I was reminded that I need to take responsibility for myself, including going out to purchase my own cigarettes if I can't go without. We also spoke about a recent incident involving another resident, which led to the police being called. I understand that if someone comes back intoxicated, the best thing for me to do is to go to my room to avoid any conflict.

We also talked about my medication. I had stopped taking my depot injections because I felt they were affecting my motivation. However, I’ve been off them for a few weeks now, and I can see that I may be doing even less than before. I've agreed to restart my medication and planned to speak to staff about taking my tablet. I understand this is important for helping me stay on track.

I was also spoken to about some of my behaviour online and towards others. I admitted to wanting to approach people in an aggressive way and mentioned that I had sent a message to a female, saying I would get my sister involved. I now understand that this kind of behaviour is not acceptable, and I've been warned that I’m getting close to serious consequences. I know I need to take more responsibility for how I act.

I’ve agreed to re-engage with support, including taking my medication again. I’m also open to reflecting more on my actions and their consequences. I am working on staying calm, especially when things trigger me in the house.
fields.action_plan:
I will talk to staff every day to confirm I’ve taken my medication.

I’ll try to walk away or go to my room if I feel triggered or annoyed by others.

I’ll work with staff during key sessions to talk about anything that’s bothering me or any behaviour that’s not okay.

I will attend my appointments and give the new medication a proper try.

I’ll make more of an effort to stay calm and not act out online or towards others.
fields.goal: My goal is to feel more stable, stay out of trouble, and avoid situations that could lead to police involvement. I also want to improve how I get along with others and use support when I need it.
fields.achievements: I’ve taken on board the concerns raised about my behaviour and the impact of stopping my medication. I’ve agreed to start taking my medication again and to work with staff to stay on track.

fields.title: Mental Health Medication Update
fields.issue:
I am currently receiving a monthly depot injection at Bridgewell House. During a 1:1 key session, I raised a concern with my key worker that I feel I may need to stop the depot. My psychiatrist and I have now booked an appointment on 20 May 2025 to discuss this further.

Following my appointment with the GP, we were able to discuss my health and medication. I expressed that I’ve been experiencing poor sleep patterns since stopping Diazepam. I also shared that I am considering stopping the depot injection, as I have been experiencing pain at the injection site, although I have not had any other side effects.

My psychiatrist advised against stopping the depot or changing the dose, as there is a high risk of relapse. We agreed to add Promethazine 25–30 mg PRN, with a maximum of 50 mg per day, to help with sleep as and when needed.
fields.action_plan:
Share all physical symptoms (e.g. injection site pain) and mental health experiences.

Continue to follow medical advice regarding medication changes or continuation.
fields.goal: To manage sleep difficulties and side effects while continuing my prescribed mental health treatment, including not stopping any medication (such as the depot injection) without medical advice.
fields.achievements: I have continued with my prescribed medication, including the depot injection, and followed medical advice. I am managing my sleep difficulties more safely with Promethazine as needed, and I have not made any changes to my medication without first speaking to my doctor or psychiatrist.

fields.issue:

I am one of the residents and I have a tenancy agreement in place which I am meant to comply with.

I struggle to manage my home environment and requires staff support to clean and tidy my room. 
I have agreed for this support to be offered every day.
I tend to manage my environment well in the communal areas and clean the communal areas after use.
I need prompting to do laundry and changing my clothes.
